articles.title: Interplay Between Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are key pathogenic drivers in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Chronic ER stress impairs epithelial barrier integrity and stimulates inflammatory pathways, causing cell death. Simultaneously, mitochondrial dysfunction results in excessive reactive oxygen species production, bioenergetic failure, and defective mitophagy, further disrupting intestinal homeostasis. Notably, these two organellar stress responses are physically and functionally linked via mitochondria-ER contacts (MERCs), which form signaling platforms-mitochondria-associated ER membranes. These platforms coordinate calcium transfer and redox signaling while integrating autophagy and the unfolded protein response (UPR). This review comprehensively summarizes the current molecular mechanisms by which ER stress and mitochondrial dysfunction aid IBD pathogenesis, emphasizing calcium homeostasis imbalance, oxidative stress, disrupted mitochondrial quality control, and autophagy-UPR integration. Furthermore, this article highlights the functional interplay between the ER and mitochondria, as well as the MERCs that structurally connect them. Additionally, it discusses emerging diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies based on these mechanisms, aiming to offer theoretical insights and novel perspectives for IBD research and clinical intervention.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Lipid Droplet-Mitochondria Interactions and Their Roles in Diseases.
articles.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) coordinate cellular lipid utilization, energy homeostasis, redox balance, and autophagy through dynamic inter-organelle communication with mitochondria. This review summarized recent advances in the molecular mechanisms regulating LD-mitochondria interactions and discusses how their dysregulation contributes to disease progression. Accumulating evidence has indicated that the contacts between LD and mitochondria are dynamically regulated through specialized membrane contact sites and protein complexes, such as Perilipin (PLIN) family of proteins, Mitofusin2 (Mfn2), and Rab GTPases. Rather than being a passive structural association, this interaction serves as a regulatory hub that integrates fatty acid (FA) transport, metabolic adaptation, and stress responses. It enables bidirectional regulation of lipid metabolism, allowing cells to flexibly and efficiently switch between lipid storage and FA oxidation in response to metabolic signals. Disruption of this inter-organelle communication impairs intracellular lipid utilization, compromises mitochondrial function, and exacerbates oxidative stress and ferroptosis. Such dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a core mechanism underlying metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases and neurodegenerative diseases. In the future, integration of protein regulation, gene editing technologies, and precision therapeutic approaches may enable specific targeting of LD-mitochondria communication, thereby offering new avenues for the treatment of relevant diseases.

articles.title: Therapeutic efficacy and dosing regimen evidence synthesis of Ursolic Acid for liver injury: A preclinical systematic review with machine learning.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ursolic acid (UA), a pentacyclic triterpene, shows hepatoprotective efficacy and favorable safety in various animal models of liver injury. However, robust preclinical evidence remains scarce. PURPOSE: To synthesize the preclinical evidence for UA and explore how UA dose and treatment duration are associated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) improvement in animal models of liver injury. STUDY DESIGN: This preclinical systematic review integrating meta-analysis and machine learning followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). METHODS: Relevant preclinical studies through April 11, 2026 were systematically retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, OVID, CNKI and Wanfang. Machine learning analyses were used to identify factors associated with ALT improvement, particularly human equivalent dose (HED) and treatment duration. RESULTS: Forty-seven articles were included in this analysis. UA markedly improved histopathological parameters, liver function, biochemical parameters, serum lipid levels, oxidative stress indicators, and inflammatory markers in liver injury animal models. Random forest was selected as the final predictive model. The analysis further identified model administration route, treatment duration, HED, and time of administration as key determinants for the improvement rate of ALT. An exploratory HED range of approximately 5-7 mg/kg was associated with greater predicted ALT improvement. CONCLUSION: The study indicates that UA exerts hepatoprotective effects in animal models of liver injury. Potential mechanisms include modulation of the gut-liver axis, attenuation of hepatic and systemic oxidative stress, and suppression of inflammation and fibrosis. Given the exploratory nature of these preclinical findings, the translational potential of UA warrants further rigorous validation.

articles.title: Scalable cultured gut microbiota-derived nanovesicles for oral augmentation of checkpoint blockade therapy.
articles.abstract: Microbiota-targeted strategies, such as fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), hold promise for enhancing immunotherapy but face clinical challenges including safety risks, batch-to-batch variability, and dependence on substantial quantities of donor fecal material. To overcome these limitations, we established a standardized in vitro expansion platform for responder patient-derived gut microbiota. Through optimization of culture conditions, we achieved stable viability and retention of key immunotherapy-enhancing strains over serial passages, enabling a scalable 6.4 × 107-fold expansion. Leveraging this platform, we engineered hybrid nanovesicles derived from bacterial protoplasts, followed by silica surface coating (HNVs@Silica) for oral delivery. The silica shell significantly improved nanovesicle stability under gastrointestinal conditions and conferred superior antitumor efficacy compared with uncoated counterparts. Notably, HNVs@Silica produced from the 2nd, 4th, and 6th passages retained comparable potency in augmenting anti-PD-1 (αPD-1) therapy. Mechanistically, HNVs@Silica remodeled intestinal immunity, particularly within Peyer's patches, by activating and expanding effector CD8+ T cells. This local response enhanced the priming and systemic dissemination of tumor-specific T cells, thereby improving the efficacy of αPD-1. Collectively, our findings establish a safe, scalable, and orally bioavailable alternative to FMT for enhancing cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Phenylboronate hydrogel for administration route tailored dual-drug delivery to anterior and posterior ocular segments.
articles.abstract: Frequent multidrug eyedrop instillation for ocular perioperative prophylaxis (e.g., cataract surgery) suffers from rapid nasolacrimal clearance, limited corneal penetration, and poor access to the posterior segment. To address these limitations, we engineered an interface-adaptive phenylboronate ester hydrogel for rapid in situ gelation and the co-entrapment of two frequently instilled drugs (moxifloxacin and dexamethasone) in their free or liposomal forms at physiological pH. This platform utilizes chemical crosslinking between hyaluronic acid-conjugated 2-aminophenylboronic acid and the diols of polyvinyl alcohol (HA-2APBA@PVA), forming a dynamic hydrogel network via phenylboronate ester bonds with a thermodynamically favorable formation energy (ΔG = -10.64 kcal/mol). This unique chemistry imparts shear-thinning injectability through fine ophthalmic needles, ensures mechanical stability against blink-induced shearing, and drives robust mucoadhesion with tear film mucins such as MUC5AC for prolonged ocular retention at the injection site. Architecturally, a "liposome-in-gel" system establishes hierarchical diffusion steps that suppress the initial burst effect and extend drug release duration by >2-fold compared to the free-drug solution control. The hydrogel demonstrates excellent ophthalmic compatibility, exhibiting physiological osmolality, >80% optical transmittance, and near 100% viability in human corneal and retinal pigment epithelial cells. Safety was further validated via Draize irritation testing and preserved ocular histology across topical and periocular administration routes. Unlike the rapid washout of standard eyedrops, this hydrogel depot ensures prolonged ocular surface retention. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed route-dependent versatility: compared to standard eyedrops, subconjunctival administration enhanced anterior segment exposure of moxifloxacin and dexamethasone by 14.9- and 8.6-fold, respectively, while sub-Tenon dosing facilitated targeted delivery to the posterior segment. This single, dynamic covalent chemistry provides a scalable, clinically compatible alternative strategy to eyedrops and advances multidrug therapies across both ocular segments.

articles.title: A nanocomposite hydrogel enabling spatial redox compartmentalization for endogenous Cu(I) hijacking and durable cuproptosis-mediated tumor vaccination.
articles.abstract: Cuproptosis-based in situ tumor vaccination provides a unique opportunity to transform tumor destruction into systemic antitumor immunity. However, the oxidative stress required for efficient tumor killing simultaneously disrupts immune competence through copper toxicity and immunosuppressive remodeling. Herein, we develop a spatial redox compartmentalized nanocomposite hydrogel platform to resolve this paradox by selectively amplifying intracellular cuproptosis while preserving the extracellular immune niche. Following peritumoral co-injection of gallic acid-grafted chitosan (CS-GA), dopamine-grafted oxidized hyaluronic acid (OHA-DA), and neocuproine-caffeic acid (NCP-CA) nanoparticles, the hydrogel establishes distinct redox microdomains for tumor eradication and immune protection. Specifically, NCP selectively exploits endogenous exchangeable Cu(I) pools and redirects copper toward mitochondria, where copper valence transformation and ferredoxin 1-mediated activation induce dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase oligomerization, mitochondrial proteotoxic stress, and cuproptotic immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, CA treatment was associated with increased AMPK phosphorylation and a 63.5% reduction in PD-L1 expression. Simultaneously, catechol-mediated redox cycling by CS-GA&OHA-DA continuously scavenges extracellular reactive oxygen species, alleviating oxidative immunosuppression and restoring T-cell viability to 94.4%. After 14 days of treatment, a substantial tumor regression was observed with a tumor volume reduction exceeding 64.2%. In a contralateral tumor rechallenge model, enhanced infiltration of CD8+ T-cells (40.8%) and CD8+ TEM-cells (26.4%) contributed to 75.6% inhibition of tumor recurrence and 93.3% suppression of metastasis. By exploiting endogenous copper resources rather than exogenous copper supplementation and spatially decoupling tumoricidal oxidation from immune-protective antioxidation, this hydrogel platform establishes a new approach for cuproptosis-based in situ vaccination, inducing durable antitumor immune memory and effectively preventing postoperative tumor recurrence and metastasis.

articles.title: Lentinan-induced FUBP1 O-GlcNAcylation suppresses macrophage ferroptosis and atherosclerosis via the Tp53/SLC7A11 axis.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis remains a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, driven by macrophage dysfunction and necrotic core expansion. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death, is a critical driver of plaque instability; however, pharmacological interventions targeting ferroptosis remain scarce. Lentinan (LNT), a bioactive β-(1,3)-glucan extracted from shiitake mushrooms, exhibits potent antioxidant properties but its potential role in the modulation of macrophage ferroptosis remains unexplored. We investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of action of LNT in atherosclerosis. LNT administration significantly attenuated atherosclerotic progression in mice. Specifically, LNT mitigated macrophage ferroptosis by enhancing glutathione homeostasis and reducing lipid peroxidation. Notably, these protective effects were significantly abrogated in mice deficient in solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), indicating that the effect of LNT is dependent on this molecule. We found that LNT directly binds to far upstream binding protein 1 (FUBP1) and that T559 is required for FUBP1 O-GlcNAcylation and subsequent nuclear translocation. In the nucleus, FUBP1 binds to tumor protein p53 (Tp53), thereby relieving the transcriptional repression of SLC7A11. The resulting activation of the SLC7A11 signaling axis not only inhibits ferroptosis but also promotes scavenger receptor B type 1 (SR-B1)-mediated cholesterol efflux. These findings highlight LNT as a novel modulator of the FUBP1/Tp53/SLC7A11 axis, offering a promising natural therapeutic strategy to stabilize atherosclerotic plaques.

articles.title: SLMO2 Promotes Chemoresistance in Glioblastoma by Regulating BNIP3-Dependent Mitophagy via the NF-κB/HIF-1α Axis.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive malignancy, with chemoresistance acting as a major hurdle that severely limits clinical efficacy and long-term prognosis. Mitophagy, a core mechanism of mitochondrial quality control, enables tumor cells to adapt to chemotherapy-induced stress and maintain survival. However, its regulatory mechanism in GBM chemoresistance remains poorly understood. Here, we identify SLMO2 as a key factor mediating chemoresistance in GBM. Low-dose TMZ induces protective mitophagy, whereas SLMO2 knockdown abrogates this autophagic defense, thereby sensitizing GBM cells to TMZ-induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, TMZ treatment upregulates SLMO2, which potently activates HIF-1α signaling to transcriptionally drive BNIP3-mediated mitophagy, a process dependent on ROS-NF-κB signaling. Notably, this SLMO2-mediated cascade is also engaged under cisplatin-induced stress, indicating a broader role in chemoresistance. Collectively, our findings reveal that SLMO2 promotes chemoresistance in GBM by regulating BNIP3-mediated mitophagy. Targeting SLMO2 disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis by this process, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for enhancing chemosensitivity in GBM.

articles.title: Tumor-on-chip and cancer microphysiological platforms: knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and the emergence of organoid-integrated models, 2010-2025.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer microphysiological systems (MPS), including tumor-on-chip platforms, combine engineered microenvironments, controlled fluid transport, and tumor-relevant biological models for cancer modeling, drug testing, and translational research. Organoid-integrated chips represent one developing component within this broader field, but the publication growth, knowledge structure, and changing research priorities of cancer MPS and tumor-on-chip research have not been systematically mapped across major bibliographic databases. METHODS: We performed a dual-database bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus from 2010 to 2025. Bibliometric indicators were analyzed using Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. We examined publication growth, source distribution, author and country collaboration, highly cited and co-cited references, and temporal keyword evolution. In addition, a phase-split keyword analysis was conducted to compare the research emphasis during 2010-2020 and 2021-2025. RESULTS: A total of 476 publications were included in the final cancer MPS/tumor-on-chip corpus. Research output increased markedly after 2020 and reached 101 articles in 2025. Source, co-citation, and keyword analyses suggested a progressive shift from early emphasis on microfluidic device construction and physical culture control toward greater attention to biofabrication, tumor microenvironment reconstruction, immune-related interactions, and drug-screening and other application-oriented themes. Phase-split keyword analysis showed that recent publications placed greater attention on biological applications and translational questions while retaining a clear connection with earlier engineering-oriented research. The United States and China emerged as the major research hubs, although with different collaboration profiles. CONCLUSION: This study provides a dual-database bibliometric analysis of cancer microphysiological systems and tumor-on-chip research from 2010 to 2025. The field has expanded from microfluidic engineering and basic tumor reconstruction toward tumor microenvironment modeling, multicellular interactions, drug-related applications, and organoid integration. These trends indicate growing translational interest, although the biological performance and clinical utility of individual platforms require direct experimental evaluation.

articles.title: Efficacy of plant extracts for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide, affecting approximately 38% of the global population. This network meta-analysis systematically compared the effects of different plant extracts on liver biochemical and non-invasive histological outcomes in patients with MASLD. METHODS: This study was performed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251229711). We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to November 12, 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing plant extracts in adults with MASLD. Primary outcomes were alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness measurement (LSM), and hepatic steatosis percentage. Network meta-analyses were conducted using Stata 15.1 and R 4.2.1. RESULTS: In total, 32 RCTs were included, involving 2,053 patients and 28 types of plant extracts. For liver enzyme outcomes, a novel curcumin preparation (CP) exhibited the highest ranking probability for ALT reduction (SUCRA: 91.93%), whereas cinnamon (Cin) ranked highest for AST reduction (SUCRA: 88.48%). For non-invasive histological outcomes, purslane (Pur) showed the greatest ranking probability for reducing LSM (SUCRA: 94.16%), while fenugreek (Fen) demonstrated favorable ranking probabilities for both CAP reduction (SUCRA: 79.07%) and hepatic steatosis percentage reduction (SUCRA: 86.97%). The overall methodological quality of the included studies was generally acceptable, and funnel plot assessments revealed no substantial evidence of publication bias. CONCLUSION: Compared with placebo, most plant extracts do not achieve statistically significant improvements in liver biochemical or non-invasive liver-related outcomes, leaving their overall clinical efficacy uncertain. Although CP, Cin, Fen, and Pur showed favorable probability rankings for specific endpoints based on SUCRA values, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinically meaningful superiority. Given the limited evidence, considerable heterogeneity, and uncertainty in comparative estimates, the current data do not support the use of plant extracts as standalone therapies for MASLD outside the context of concomitant lifestyle modification. Adequately powered, standardized RCTs are warranted to clarify their therapeutic effects. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251229711; Identifier: CRD420251229711.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of P2X3 receptor antagonists in refractory or unexplained chronic cough: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Refractory chronic cough and unexplained chronic cough are increasingly understood as clinical expressions of cough hypersensitivity. P2X3 receptor antagonists have been developed to reduce ATP-mediated airway sensory nerve activation, but their benefit must be balanced against taste-related adverse events. METHODS: Randomized placebo-controlled trials evaluating oral P2X3 receptor antagonists in adults with refractory or unexplained chronic cough were included. Objective cough frequency and taste-related adverse events were selected as primary efficacy and safety/tolerability outcomes. Secondary outcomes included Leicester Cough Questionnaire (LCQ) total score, cough severity visual analogue scale (VAS), overall adverse events, and discontinuation due to adverse events. Effects were pooled using random-effects inverse-variance models. Sensitivity analyses, publication-bias assessment, and GRADE certainty ratings were performed. RESULTS: Eleven trial reports involving 3568 participants were included, yielding 13 independent comparisons for objective cough frequency. P2×3 receptor antagonists reduced objective cough frequency compared with placebo (ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.63-0.79), corresponding to a 29.3% relative reduction. They also improved LCQ total score (MD 1.44, 95% CI 0.78-2.09) and cough severity VAS (MD -12.73 mm, 95% CI -17.10 to -8.36). Taste-related adverse events were increased (RR 7.36, 95% CI 4.84-11.21), as were overall adverse events (RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.07-1.38) and discontinuation due to adverse events (RR 3.62, 95% CI 2.65-4.93). Leave-one-out analyses did not alter the direction of any pooled estimate. Egger and Begg tests suggested small-study effects for objective cough frequency, but not for safety outcomes with sufficient comparisons. The certainty of evidence was rated as moderate for all prespecified outcomes. CONCLUSION: P2×3 receptor antagonists were associated with reductions in objective cough frequency and improvements in patient-reported outcomes in refractory or unexplained chronic cough. These benefits should be balanced against increased safety and tolerability concerns, especially taste disturbance, although receptor selectivity appears to attenuate this risk. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261422476.

articles.title: Transcriptomic effects of lead on the differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into ectoderm: implication for adverse pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopmental disorders.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological studies revealed associations between maternal lead (Pb) exposure and adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes as well as neurodevelopmental disorders. However, the underlying mechanisms remained unclear, and thus was investigated at the transcriptional level in this study using human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Differentiation of hESCs to ectoderm was induced for 7 days using STEMdiff™ Trilineage Differentiation Kit containing 0 (water), 6.2 (geometric mean concentration of Pb in human maternal blood), or 118 µg Pb2+/L, in the form of lead chloride (PbCl2), followed by bulk RNA sequencing. Both doses of PbCl2 altered gene expression related to protein metabolism and trafficking, while also causing changes in genes involved in gastrulation, proliferation, DNA repair, stress response, and immune-cell development. PbCl2 at the low dose induced gene changes predicting decreased cell proliferation and increased sensory loss. Cells exposed to the high dose of PbCl2 had a distinct global gene expression profile from that of control cells with specific changes predicting increased neurodegeneration. The differences in expression of ectoderm lineage marker genes (ELMG) between control and PbCl2 treated cells did not reach statistical significance. However, expression of some genes downstream of ELMG differed markedly between control and PbCl2 treated cells. Multiple adverse outcome pathways involving WNT, IGF-1, RHO-PKN, CDK5, MAP kinase, and Ca2+ signaling, cell cycle control, protein metabolism and trafficking, DNA double strand break and repair, and immune response were detected in PbCl2 treated cells. Overall, the findings suggest that Pb exposure disrupted early ectodermal development by prioritizing genome preservation over fate execution.

articles.title: The role of sitagliptin in modifying metabolic, hormonal and clinical parameters in polycystic ovarian syndrome patients: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a disease that is not limited to reproductive symptoms; it is also significantly linked to metabolic problems such as obesity, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor, may play a significant role in metabolic, inflammatory, and hormonal abnormalities in PCOS patients. OBJECTIVE: This randomized clinical trial aimed to investigate the impact of sitagliptin on metabolic disturbances, hormonal abnormalities, and clinical outcomes in patients with PCOS. The study is registered on Clinicaltrials.gov with an ID of (NCT05972928). METHODS: This randomized controlled trial was conducted at Beni-Suef University Hospital, involving 80 women diagnosed with PCOS based on the Rotterdam criteria. Participants were equally allocated into either a sitagliptin group, receiving 100 mg daily, or a control group, with a follow-up period of 3 months. Changes in body weight served as the sole primary outcome of the study. Meanwhile, changes in BMI, HOMA-IR, lipid profile, and hormonal indicators, along with clinical improvements in infertility, hirsutism, acne, and menstrual irregularity, were evaluated as secondary outcomes. RESULTS: Regarding the primary outcome, a highly significant reduction in body weight was observed within the sitagliptin group (p < 0.001). Similarly, secondary outcomes including BMI, HOMA-IR, DHEA, HbA1c, total and free testosterone, and LH levels, all demonstrated significant decreases (p < 0.05). Clinical secondary outcomes also showed potential improvements, with menstrual regularity increasing significantly (p = 0.006), alongside visible reductions in hirsutism (p = 0.006) and exploratory reduction in the infertility rates (p = 0.031), that needs further confirmation. Furthermore, the intervention was well-tolerated, as recorded side effects were both rare and mild in intensity. CONCLUSION: Sitagliptin has potential impact on the hormonal, metabolic and clinical aspects of PCOS, and an exploratory effect on reproductive function. This makes it a potentially promising option for managing this complex condition. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05972928, identifier NCT05972928.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison. CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

articles.title: Semi-solid extrusion 3D printing for personalized drug delivery: rheology, printability, and pharmaceutical applications.
articles.abstract: Conventional pharmaceutical manufacturing is optimized for standardized fixed-dose products and offers limited flexibility for patients requiring individualized dosing, patient-acceptable dosage forms, or multidrug therapy. Semi-solid extrusion (SSE) 3D printing can process gels, pastes, suspensions, and other viscoelastic formulations under mild thermal conditions to produce dosage forms with digitally controlled dose, geometry, and drug-release behavior. This review summarizes recent advances in pharmaceutical SSE 3D printing from formulation, process, application, and translational perspectives. Key rheological determinants of printability are discussed, including yield-related behavior, shear-thinning behavior, viscoelasticity, and structural recovery, which collectively influence extrudability, filament deposition, shape retention, and structural fidelity. Current printability assessment strategies are also reviewed, with emphasis on linking ink properties and printing parameters to critical quality attributes such as dimensional accuracy, content uniformity, mechanical integrity, dissolution and drug-release performance, and stability. Pharmaceutical applications are discussed in individualized dose adjustment, structure-mediated release modulation, medicines for pediatric and older adult, non-oral and local delivery systems, implantable formulations, and multidrug products. Finally, translational requirements are considered, including validated digital workflows, qualified manufacturing processes, process analytical technologies, appropriate quality monitoring, microbial control, packaging, and auditable regulatory documentation. Overall, SSE 3D printing represents a promising platform with substantial potential for personalized drug delivery, although broader clinical implementation will require stronger clinical, regulatory, and health-economic evidence.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine inhibits gene and protein expression of MUC5AC in COPD-relevant human models: evidence from a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Chronic mucus hypersecretion is highly prevalent in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and is associated with worse outcomes. MUC5AC is a key inducible gel-forming mucin driving pathological mucus overproduction. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is widely used as a mucolytic and exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Its quantitative impact on MUC5AC regulation has not been formally synthesized. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis (OSF registration ID: 2vym4) of original studies evaluating the effect of NAC on MUC5AC gene and protein expression in human respiratory cell models of mucus hypersecretion. Standardized mean differences with 95% CIs were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Heterogeneity, publication bias, sensitivity analyses, and random-effects meta-regression on NAC dose were conducted. Fifteen articles were included. NAC significantly reduced MUC5AC mRNA (standardized mean difference -1.30, 95% CI: -1.61 to -0.98; I2=37.07%), without significant dose-response. NAC produced very large reductions in extracellular (-2.70, 95% CI: -3.29 to -2.11; I2=48.89%) and intracellular (-2.38, 95% CI: -3.27 to -1.48; I2=67.35%) MUC5AC protein, with significant dose-response relationships for both. After sensitivity analyses, the pooled protein effect remained very large (-2.00, 95% CI: -2.38 to -1.62; I2=25.63%). Funnel plots and Egger's tests suggested publication bias, which diminished after exclusion of influential comparisons. NAC robustly inhibits MUC5AC gene and protein expression in human pre-clinical models of mucus hypersecretion, supporting a strong mucoregulatory action that complements mucolytic and antioxidant effects. These data reinforce the rationale for NAC use in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients with a hypersecretory phenotype.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning, a game changer in pharmaceutical development ? - An updated perspective arising from Journees Galeniques 2024.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being applied across pharmaceutical development, from drug-property prediction and safety assessment to formulation design, model-informed development and clinical research. This perspective synthesizes discussions from Journées Galéniques 2024 and updates them in light of scientific and regulatory developments through 2026. ML enables prediction, pattern recognition, and data-driven decision-making, helping researchers identify drug targets, design new molecules, predict toxicity, and optimize drug properties. In formulation development, ML can improve solubility prediction, excipient selection, and formulation strategy by reducing trial-and-error approaches. AI-based models and imaging technologies can also enhance understanding of drug delivery systems and improve prediction of in vivo performance. However, much of the published literature remains retrospective and is based on small or heterogeneous datasets, with limited external, prospective or clinically relevant validation. Recent regulatory frameworks place increasing emphasis on a clearly defined context of use, risk-based assessment of model credibility, data governance, generalizability, human oversight and lifecycle management. AI and ML should therefore be viewed not as replacements for pharmaceutical science, but as increasingly powerful tools that can strengthen and accelerate it. Their broader impact will depend on high-quality, interoperable data, rigorous validation, integration with pharmaceutical and clinical expertise, and clear evidence of meaningful clinical, manufacturing or regulatory value.

articles.title: Protective effects and possible mechanisms of Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions in animal models of osteoarthritis: a preclinical systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge, commonly known as Danshen, is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb historically used for blood stasis- and pain-related disorders. Its extracts and bioactive constituents have shown anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and tissue-protective effects, suggesting potential value for osteoarthritis (OA). AIM OF THE STUDY: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the protective effects and possible mechanisms of Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions in animal models of OA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to March 2026. Controlled in vivo animal studies assessing Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions or related constituents in OA models were included. Primary outcomes were histological cartilage damage scores, including OARSI and Mankin scores. Secondary outcomes included inflammatory cytokines, cartilage matrix metabolism markers, apoptosis-related indicators, and oxidative stress markers. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 456 animals were included. Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions significantly attenuated histological cartilage damage, as reflected by lower OARSI scores (SMD = -4.20, 95% CI -5.31 to -3.09; I2 = 69.26%) and Mankin scores (SMD = -6.50, 95% CI -8.50 to -4.50; I2 = 85.61%). Model type showed a significant subgroup difference for OARSI score, and intervention category showed a significant subgroup difference for Mankin score, suggesting possible sources of heterogeneity. Significant reductions were observed in serum IL-1β, serum IL-6, cartilage/chondrocyte IL-6, and serum TNF-α, whereas the reduction in cartilage TNF-α did not reach statistical significance. Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions also increased Aggrecan and Collagen II expression and modulated MMP-13 expression, supporting an improvement in cartilage matrix homeostasis. Apoptosis-related analyses showed increased Bcl-2 expression and reduced caspase-3 expression and TUNEL-positive apoptotic cells, whereas the reduction in Bax expression was not statistically significant. Cartilage MDA levels were also significantly reduced. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis indicated that the pooled OARSI result was robust. Although funnel plot asymmetry was observed, trim-and-fill analysis did not alter the direction of the pooled effect. CONCLUSIONS: Current preclinical evidence suggests that Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions may attenuate cartilage structural damage in animal models of OA, with possible involvement of inflammatory responses, extracellular matrix metabolism, chondrocyte apoptosis, and oxidative stress. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity across several outcomes, small sample sizes, limited numbers of studies for several mechanistic endpoints, wide uncertainty in some model-based sensitivity analyses, and incomplete reporting of key methodological safeguards. Overall, these results support further investigation of Salvia miltiorrhiza-derived interventions in OA-related preclinical research, but more rigorously designed, standardized, and independently replicated animal studies are needed before clinical translation can be considered.

articles.title: Sirtuin 1-microRNA regulatory networks in liver diseases: Mechanistic convergence, cellular senescence, and translational implications.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, hepatotoxicity, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma are stages of chronic liver injury that occur in the setting of complex interactions of the various factors, including metabolic dysregulation, inflammation, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence. Recent studies propose that microRNAs (miRNAs), regulators of these processes, act through modulation of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), a key metabolic and stress-response sensor recognizing the organism's needs under various physiological and pathological conditions. Abnormalities in the SIRT1-miRNA network function are implicated in processes of lipid accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, immune-cell activation, stellate-cell transdifferentiation, fibrogenesis, and tumor development. In the present review, we make an attempt to carry out joint analysis of SIRT1-miRNA interaction throughout the history of liver diseases. In contrast to the previously existing reviews focusing on independent miRNAs and diseases independently, we focus on the idea of mechanistic convergence and the specificity of how SIRT1 works in different disease stages. We also consider novel ideas, including the concept of cellular senescence, immunometabolic switch, communication through exosomes, and the role of SIRT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma development. We analyze the way the regulation of SIRT1 by miRNA affects metabolic adaptation and fibrogenesis. Although experimental studies consistently support the biological significance of the SIRT1-miRNA axis, important translational challenges remain, including disease heterogeneity, cell-specific targeting, delivery limitations, and insufficient clinical validation. Future integration of multiomics technologies, circulating miRNA biomarkers, and precision-medicine approaches may improve understanding of SIRT1-centered regulatory networks and facilitate the development of more effective therapeutic strategies for liver diseases. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: By investigating the intricacies of sirtuin 1-microRNA (SIRT1-miRNA) regulatory mechanisms, valuable knowledge is gained regarding the role of SIRT1 post-transcriptional regulation in causing metabolic disorders, inflammation, fibrosis, and progression of hepatocellular carcinoma. The article also highlights serious pharmacological challenges in this area, such as specificity of treatment, possible influence of drugs on other mechanisms of the body, and ability to separate the beneficial effects of SIRT1 activation in the case of metabolic liver disease from its harmful effects in more advanced cases of hepatocellular carcinoma.

articles.title: Advances in androgenetic alopecia model research.
articles.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most prevalent form of non-scarring hair loss, and its pathogenesis is quite complex, involving androgen metabolism, follicular microenvironment imbalance, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Understanding these multifactorial mechanisms is critical for developing effective therapeutic strategies. To this end, various experimental models have been extensively employed. In this review, we summarized recent progress in AGA model research, covering in vitro cell models such as dermal papilla cells and keratinocytes, in vivo animal models-primarily mice treated with testosterone or dihydrotestosterone, as well as genetically modified strains, and ex vivo hair follicle organ culture models. Some emerging approaches, like three-dimensional organoid systems and Organ-on-a-Chip Technologies, are also discussed. The aim of this review is to provide a theoretical framework to guide future drug development and mechanistic studies in AGA.

articles.title: Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome in rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes: pathogenic mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovitis, pannus formation, cartilage degradation, and bone erosion. Although conventional synthetic, biologic, and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs have improved disease control, many patients fail to achieve sustained remission, lose responsiveness over time, or develop treatment-limiting safety concerns. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) are increasingly recognized as long-lived pathogenic stromal cells that sustain synovial inflammation, promote matrix degradation, support osteoclastogenesis, and shape immune and vascular crosstalk within the rheumatoid joint. The NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome provides a mechanistic link between synovial stress responses and inflammatory amplification. In RA-FLSs, defined inflammatory, hypoxic and oxidative-stress conditions can induce NLRP3-related signaling, whereas other proposed triggers, including lysosomal injury, extracellular ATP and ion flux, are supported more strongly by broader synovial or general inflammasome evidence. Through caspase-1 activation, interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 maturation, and gasdermin D-mediated pyroptotic signaling, NLRP3 can reinforce stromal inflammation and tissue-destructive synovial remodeling. In this review, we summarize canonical, non-canonical, and alternative mechanisms of NLRP3 inflammasome activation, with emphasis on their relevance to RA-FLS biology and the inflamed synovial niche. We discuss how NLRP3 signaling intersects with fibroblast heterogeneity, macrophage-FLS crosstalk, endothelial activation, chondrocyte injury, osteoclastogenesis, and context-dependent pyroptosis. We further evaluate pharmacological strategies targeting the NLRP3 axis, including direct NLRP3 inhibitors, upstream stress modulators, caspase-1 or gasdermin D blockade, IL-1β/IL-18 pathway inhibition, natural products, repurposed molecules, nanomedicine-based delivery, and rational combination regimens. Key translational issues include FLS specificity, synovial drug exposure, target engagement, chronic safety, biomarker-guided patient selection, and mechanism-aligned endpoints. An RA-FLS-centered view of NLRP3 targeting may help refine anti-inflammatory pharmacology and support the development of synovium-directed therapeutic strategies for selected patients with difficult-to-treat RA.

articles.title: Plant-derived modulators of the hemostasis-wound healing axis: mechanisms, evidence, and translational potential.
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants are widely used to control bleeding and support wound care, but the hemostatic and reparative evidence attributed to a species often derives from different plant parts, extracts, or formulations. This critical narrative review examines the ethnomedicinal, experimental, clinical, safety, and translational evidence for plant-derived preparations reported to modulate one or more stages of the hemostasis-wound-healing axis. Structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were updated through 19 July 2026 using terms related to medicinal plants, coagulation, platelet function, wound healing, formulation, standardization, toxicity, and safety. The literature retained for detailed synthesis encompassed crude extracts, enriched fractions, latex-derived proteases, isolated plant metabolites, hydrogels, nanoparticles, and other formulated materials. Mechanistically, direct evidence was concentrated primarily in fibrinogen-cleaving plant proteases and notoginsenoside Ft1-mediated platelet signaling. In contrast, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic, antimicrobial, and extracellular-matrix-related effects were supported mainly at the extract, fraction, or formulation level. The strength and mechanistic depth of the evidence varied substantially among species, preparations, experimental models, and outcomes, and hemostatic and wound-repair effects were frequently demonstrated using different materials from the same species. Thus, the available evidence supports the hemostasis-wound-healing axis as a useful framework for prioritizing candidates, but current evidence does not support medicinal plants as a uniformly effective therapeutic class. Translation should initially prioritize chemically and biologically standardized topical or locally retained products, component-specific controls, clinically relevant preclinical models, exposure-response and safety characterization, and adequately powered indication-specific trials. Taxonomic validity, material traceability, sustainable sourcing, and ethical governance of traditional knowledge should be integrated from the outset.

articles.title: A review of protective effects of Withania somnifera and its bioactive component withaferin A in organ ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Withania somnifera (WS) is an Ayurvedic botanical which has been extensively studied for thousands of years. Withanolides are the main pharmacologically active ingredients isolated from WS and withaferin A (WA) is the most extensively studied and therapeutically effective withanolide compound. WS and WA have anti-ischemia-reperfusion injury effects. To summarize and investigate the protective roles of WS and WA and their underlying mechanisms in organ ischemia-reperfusion injury, a comprehensive literature search was conducted using databases including PubMed and Web of Science. Relevant in vitro and preclinical regarding WS and WA in the treatment of organ ischemia-reperfusion injury. By analyzing the existing research advances, we found that the anti-organ ischemia-reperfusion injury effects of WS and WA, primarily mediated through anti-apoptosis, anti-oxidative stress, anti-inflammatory, anti-mitochondrial dysfunctions, induction of neuronal regeneration and inhibition of migration. This review systematically summarizes the different roles and mechanisms of WS and WA in organ ischemia-reperfusion injury and provides a basis for future therapeutic investigation of organ ischemia/reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Thioredoxin system: mechanisms and therapeutic potential in mental disorders.
articles.abstract: Mental disorders, including depression, schizophrenia (SCZ), autism spectrum disorders (ASD), and substance use disorders (SUD), impose a substantial global disease burden. The pathogenesis of these diseases is complex and not fully understood, which limits the therapeutic efficacy of existing interventions. Cumulative evidence indicates that redox imbalance, impaired neurogenesis, neuroinflammation, neurotransmitter dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic dysfunction, and ferroptosis represent core pathological processes underlying mental disorders. The thioredoxin (Trx) system, a core machinery for intracellular redox homeostasis, comprises Trx, thioredoxin reductase (TrxR), nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH), and thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP). Multiple studies have documented the Trx system dysregulation across diverse mental disorders contributes to disease onset and progression. In this review, we summarize the structural composition and biological functions of the Trx system and discuss its possible molecular mechanisms in four major mental disorders. We also describe crosstalk between the Trx system and the glutathione (GSH) system and dissect the therapeutic prospects and translational bottlenecks of Trx-targeted pharmacological strategies. Future research directions are also outlined. Collectively, the Trx system serves as a promising candidate target for unraveling redox-dependent pathophysiological mechanisms in mental disorders. Nevertheless, multi-dimensional mechanistic and translational investigations are urgently required before Trx-based therapeutics can yield tangible clinical benefits for patients with psychiatric conditions.

articles.title: Targeting the secretory autophagy-extracellular vesicle interface: fate decisions and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: Autophagy preserves cellular homeostasis through lysosomal degradation, but its machinery also participates in extracellular release. This creates a pharmacological problem: changing autophagy or extracellular vesicle (EV) output can alter intracellular disposal, inflammatory signaling and communication between cells in different directions. This Review distinguishes lysosomal degradation, direct secretory autophagy and EV-associated release, with particular attention to cargo selection, tethering, fusion and the limits of route assignment. We define secretory autophagy during lysosome inhibition as a stress-dependent response and distinguish it from regulated secretion in physiological settings. Disease comparisons across cancer, neurodegeneration, inflammation and infection show why the source cell, cargo and recipient response matter for intervention. We evaluate three strategies: restoring degradation, suppressing harmful secretion and preserving or exploiting EV-linked communication. For representative interventions, we separate pharmacological tools from genetic candidate targets and pathway-level effects, and compare functional evidence, risks and translational maturity. Dynamic imaging, single-EV profiling and orthogonal perturbations offer complementary approaches to test route-specific effects. Current evidence supports preclinical opportunities, but does not establish clinical efficacy through a specifically validated secretory-autophagy-EV mechanism.

articles.title: AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers in precision breast cancer therapeutics: from discovery to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer is biologically heterogeneous, yet conventional clinical decisions rely on static, single-marker proxies (ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67) that capture only a narrow slice of tumor biology. This mini-review argues that AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers offer a valuable shift toward systems-level, model-derived probabilities integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and imaging information to explain and predict disease behavior more faithfully. We synthesize recent advances across three domains: (i) computational strategies for multi-omics integration, from classical penalized regression and ensemble learning to deep multimodal architectures and foundation-model embeddings; (ii) therapeutically relevant biomarker classes across tissue, liquid biopsy, and imaging modalities; and (iii) emerging pathways for embedding these biomarkers into clinical decision support. We highlight validation, interpretability, and robust handling of missing modalities as prerequisites for clinical trust, and outline how biomarker-driven trials, standardized reporting (e.g., TRIPOD + AI), and privacy-preserving data consortia can move AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers toward clinical and regulatory maturity.

articles.title: From respiratory viral infection to persistent cough hypersensitivity: neuroimmune regulation and therapeutic implications of P2X3/TRP ion-channel targets.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viral infections are increasingly recognized as important drivers of persistent airway symptoms and exacerbations in chronic lung disease. Post-infectious cough (PIC), particularly after upper respiratory tract infection, represents one of the most frequent causes of subacute cough and a mechanistically complex sequela in which cough hypersensitivity syndrome (CHS) plays a central pathophysiological role. Beyond increased cough frequency, patients with PIC frequently exhibit laryngeal sensory abnormalities and exaggerated responses to low-intensity stimuli, suggesting a sustained reduction in the activation threshold of airway sensory nerves. Among several contributors to cough hypersensitivity, P2X3 receptors and transient receptor potential (TRP) channels are key ion-channel targets mediating cough reflexes and sensory nerve hypersensitivity, yet their clinical translation has been heterogeneous. Gefapixant reduced objective cough frequency in phase III trials enrolling refractory or unexplained chronic cough populations, but these data provide indirect rather than PIC-specific evidence, and its clinical utility is limited by dysgeusia. Similarly, TRPV1 antagonists suppress capsaicin-provoked cough but have not consistently improved spontaneous cough frequency, highlighting a disconnect between provocation models and real-world post-infectious cough pathology. This review discusses how respiratory viruses may induce cough hypersensitivity through transcriptional, metabolic, and neuroimmune regulation of sensory pathways. Respiratory syncytial virus, rhinovirus, and other viral pathogens can upregulate TRPV1, TRPA1, and ASIC3 expression, while cytokines such as IFN-γ may promote sensory-neuron transcriptional reprogramming through JAK-STAT and NF-κB signaling. In parallel, inflammatory mediators including bradykinin, COX/12-LOX metabolites, and prostaglandin E2 can sensitize TRP channels through kinase-dependent phosphorylation, whereas virus-induced epithelial ATP release and impaired CD39/CD73-mediated purinergic degradation may sustain repeated P2X3 receptor activation. Persistent peripheral afferent input may further induce central sensitization, explaining residual cough despite peripheral target blockade. By integrating viral immunopathogenesis, epithelial-neural crosstalk, and ion-channel pharmacology, this review proposes a framework for understanding post-viral cough hypersensitivity as a neuroimmune sequela of respiratory infection. Future research should prioritize molecular endotype-based stratification, PIC-specific randomized controlled trials, optimization of highly selective P2X3 antagonists, and combined peripheral-central assessment strategies to guide more precise therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
articles.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, decoding their intricate polypharmacology remains a major challenge. Network pharmacology, combining multi-omics profiling, computational target prediction, and network topology, has emerged as a promising paradigm to decipher these multi-component mechanisms. Unlike previous descriptive reviews that largely focused on narrow botanical catalogs or local traditions, this review establishes a critical, globally inclusive, and methodologically rigorous synthesis of network pharmacology-driven nephrolithiasis research from 2022 to 2026. We detail the fundamental pathophysiology across major stone types (calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, uric acid, struvite, cystine) and the comprehensive cellular cascade encompassing crystal nucleation, Randall's plaque/plug formation, CD44-mediated adhesion, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species burst, endoplasmic reticulum stress, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, macrophage M1/M2 polarization, immunometabolism, extracellular vesicle communication, and programmed cell death (apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and PANoptosis). We critically synthesize evidence across diverse chemical classes (flavonoids, polyphenols, pentacyclic triterpenes, alkaloids, anthraquinones, tannins, polysaccharides, and marine bioactive metabolites), bridging computational predictions with established mechanistic milestones. Furthermore, we provide a deep critical appraisal of core methodological bottlenecks-target prediction bias, publication bias of over-studied hub genes, arbitrary pharmacokinetic cutoffs, circular virtual docking, and lack of renal bioavailability validation. Finally, we formulate a forward-looking translational roadmap integrating single-cell transcriptomics, humanized 3D organoid co-cultures, spatial multi-omics, reverse validation in longitudinal clinical registries, and machine learning feature selection, providing rigorous guidance for precision anti-urolithic drug discovery.

articles.title: Navigating neonatal thrombosis: contemporary insights into a complex disorder in a unique population.
articles.abstract: Neonatal thromboembolic disease (TE) is an increasingly recognized clinical condition associated with significant morbidity, despite its relatively low incidence in the general paediatric population. Neonates-especially those in Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs)-are at the highest risk for TE among all paediatric age groups. This elevated risk is attributed to the developmental characteristics of neonatal haemostasis, the frequent use of central venous catheters, and the presence of significant underlying comorbidities. Over recent decades, the reported incidence of neonatal TE has risen significantly, reflecting improvement in neonatal intensive care, and increased awareness and recognition of thrombotic complications. The unique pathophysiology of neonatal TE, and its distinct risk factors, underscore the need for a stronger neonatal-specific evidence to support prevention, diagnosis and management of thromboembolic events. The objective of this review is to summarise and critically appraise existing evidence on the epidemiology, the pathophysiology and the risk factors related to neonatal TE. It also aims to identify current knowledge gaps and areas requiring further investigation. Overall, the available evidence supports a multifactorial model of neonatal thrombosis, whereby developmental hemostasis interacts with acquired antenatal and perinatal risk factors. However, substantial heterogeneity in epidemiological data and diagnostic approaches continues to hinder accurate thrombotic risk stratification and evidence-based clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Circular RNAs in cancer: from biomarkers to vaccine-based immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are endogenous, covalently closed RNA molecules generated through back-splicing that exhibit exceptional stability, evolutionary conservation, tissue-specific expression and diverse regulatory functions. Compared with conventional RNA-based therapeutic platforms, such as messenger RNAs (mRNAs), small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), microRNAs (miRNAs), and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circRNAs offer enhanced resistance to exonuclease-mediated degradation, prolonged intracellular persistence, and sustained protein expression. These characteristics have positioned circRNAs as promising candidates for cancer biomarkers and next-generation therapeutic platforms. Recent evidence indicates that they regulate multiple biological processes associated with tumour initiation and progression, including transcriptional regulation, miRNA sequestration, RNA-binding protein modulation, alternative splicing, cap-independent translation, immune signalling, and therapeutic resistance. Through interactions with innate and adaptive immune pathways, circRNAs regulate antigen presentation, cytokine production, immune-cell activation and tumour immune evasion, highlighting their importance in cancer immunotherapy. This review summarizes recent advances in circRNA biogenesis and their roles in cancer progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation, with particular emphasis on engineered circRNAs as platforms for cancer vaccines and precision immunotherapy. We discuss advances in circRNA vaccine design, delivery, neoantigen targeting, biomarkers, and clinical translation, while highlighting key challenges including manufacturing, immunogenicity, tumor heterogeneity, regulatory requirements, and limited clinical validation. Overall, circRNAs represent a promising and versatile platform for cancer immunotherapy, with continued advances in RNA engineering, personalized neoantigen design, targeted delivery, and clinical evaluation expected to determine their potential for translation into effective and durable cancer treatments.

articles.title: Potential role of resveratrol in abdominal cocoon syndrome: targeting inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis via food-derived bioactive compounds resveratrol for treatment of abdominal cocoon syndrome.
articles.abstract: Abdominal cocoon syndrome (ACS) is a rare refractory peritoneal fibrotic disease marked by intestinal encapsulation by dense fibrous membranes. Its pathogenesis involves chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, immune dysregulation and peritoneal fibrosis, and targeted pharmacotherapy remains unavailable. Resveratrol, a natural medicine-food homologous polyphenol, exerts anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-angiogenic, immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic effects through NF-κB, Nrf2, TGF-β/Smad and SIRT1 pathways, showing potential as an ACS adjuvant agent. Nevertheless, poor water solubility, heavy first pass metabolism, low bioavailability, photoisomerization and biphasic dose-dependent effects greatly hinder its clinical translation. Nanocarriers, prodrugs, stimulus-responsive carriers and local intraperitoneal delivery can ameliorate these pharmacokinetic defects. Direct evidence for resveratrol against ACS is still lacking. Further studies should establish standardized ACS animal models, clarify intraperitoneal pharmacokinetics and unify raw material quality standards. Resveratrol represents a promising candidate for ACS therapy with advances in precision delivery.

articles.title: Intranasal hydrogels for Alzheimer's disease: from nasal-interface engineering to brain targeting and translational readiness.
articles.abstract: Intranasal hydrogels offer a strategy to address rapid mucociliary clearance, limited nasal residence, difficult payload properties, and insufficient brain exposure in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This Review evaluates hydrogel and hydrogel-associated systems across formulation architecture, nasal-interface performance, brain pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and translation. Selected systems improved deposition or retention, controlled release, permeation, and central exposure relative to relevant comparators, with some also showing convergent behavioral and disease-relevant biological effects in preclinical models. The strongest evidence comes from matched comparisons that distinguish route effects from the incremental contributions of carriers and hydrogels. However, rheology, deposition, targeting metrics, statistical reporting, complete-product stability, repeated-dose safety, device performance, and human reproducibility remain inconsistently characterized. Overall, the evidence supports intranasal hydrogels as a credible preclinical platform for brain-directed AD drug delivery, but not as clinically validated therapy, and favors standardized, device-integrated, comparator-resolved development.

articles.title: Differential functions of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in liver fibrosis and advances in targeted therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis, driven by metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and other chronic injuries, represents a global health crisis without approved pharmacological therapies. The Rho-associated coiled-coil kinases (ROCK1 and ROCK2), the principal effectors of Rho GTPases, have emerged as central nodes in fibrogenesis, yet the isoform-specific mechanisms and their translational potential remain incompletely defined. This review systematically dissects the divergent roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 across the hepatic cellular landscape. We synthesize current knowledge on isoform-specific functions across major hepatic cell types, including hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), hepatocytes, macrophages, and immune cells, with emphasis on the evidence quality underlying each claim. ROCK2 appears to play a predominant role in the profibrotic vascular niche in several contexts, particularly in LSEC capillarization and HSC contraction; however, the contributions of both isoforms are fundamentally cell- and context-dependent. We discuss the evidence for ROCK isoform-specific functions, distinguishing among genetic, pharmacological, expression-based, and activation-based evidence. We further synthesize the complex crosstalk between ROCK signaling and the TGF-β/Smad, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo/YAP, and NOX4/ROS networks. Crucially, we critically evaluate the translational pipeline-from pan-ROCK inhibitors limited by systemic hypotension to next-generation selective ROCK2 inhibitors. A notable development in clinical translation is the selective ROCK2 inhibitor TDI01, which targets endothelial ROCK2 to attenuate fibrosis. In an extended, single-arm, open-label study of TDI01 in patients with liver fibrosis, fibrosis improvement was observed in five of six patients; however, given the small sample size, absence of a control group, and exploratory endpoints, these findings represent early signals that require validation in adequately powered randomized controlled trials. We further address unresolved controversies, including the dual hepatoprotective versus pro-steatotic functions of ROCK and the dose-dependent bidirectional regulation of HSCs migration, which challenge systemic inhibition strategies. Looking forward, we spotlight emerging frontiers such as cell-specific nanodelivery systems (vitamin A-liposomes, M6PHSA), PROTAC-mediated ROCK degradation, non-coding RNA therapeutics, and synergistic combinations with FXR, PPAR, and GLP-1 receptor agonists. This review provides a comprehensive blueprint for translating ROCK isoform biology into precision antifibrotic therapies.

articles.title: Cannabinoids in oncology: pharmacology, clinical applications, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Cannabis and cannabinoid products are increasingly used by patients with cancer for symptom management and supportive care. Although cannabis is widely used to alleviate cancer- and treatment-related symptoms, many patients also believe that it possesses direct anticancer activity. This review provides a comprehensive pharmacologic and clinical assessment of cannabinoids in oncology, integrating the endocannabinoid system, cannabinoid receptor signaling, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic applications, adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, and emerging antitumor research. The strongest clinical evidence supports selected cannabinoid preparations for refractory chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, whereas evidence for cancer-related pain, appetite stimulation, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and opioid-sparing effects remains limited or inconsistent. Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) differ substantially in receptor pharmacology, psychoactive effects, metabolism, and toxicity, with important implications for product selection, dosing, and interactions with anticancer and supportive-care medications. Preclinical studies demonstrate antiproliferative, proapoptotic, antiangiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects across multiple tumor models; however, cannabinoid signaling is highly context dependent and may also promote tumor progression in selected settings. Human evidence for direct anticancer activity remains sparse, consisting predominantly of small early-phase studies and observational data, with no established improvement in tumor response, progression-free survival, or overall survival. Particular caution is warranted regarding neuropsychiatric and cardiovascular toxicity, pharmacokinetic drug interactions, and the potential influence of cannabis on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Overall, cannabinoids have defined but limited roles in supportive oncology, while their direct antitumor potential remains investigational. Future studies should prioritize standardized formulations, pharmacologically informed dosing, rigorous randomized designs, clinically meaningful endpoints, and biomarker-based approaches to define therapeutic benefit and risk.

articles.title: Efsubaglutide Alfa: A Comprehensive Pharmacological Review.
articles.abstract: Efsubaglutide alfa (also known as supaglutide) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) engineered as a GLP-1 analogue fused to a human immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) fragment crystallisable (Fc) domain. This narrative review summarises published and publicly available evidence on efsubaglutide alfa pharmacology, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, dose-exposure-response relationships, drug-drug interaction potential, and clinical efficacy and safety in type 2 diabetes (T2D) and overweight/obesity. Efsubaglutide alfa has prolonged exposure (terminal half-life approximately 182-215 h) and low steady-state fluctuation, but dosing-interval selection should not be inferred from half-life alone. Available population pharmacokinetic and exposure-response analyses indicate that steady-state trough concentration is most informative for glycaemic response, whereas average and peak concentrations contribute to interpretation of weight response and gastrointestinal tolerability. Across available studies, predominantly conducted in Chinese populations, efsubaglutide alfa shows class-consistent improvements in glycaemic control and body weight, with gastrointestinal adverse events as the main tolerability limitation. Exploratory every 2-week dosing and post-discontinuation glycaemic durability findings remain hypothesis-generating. No head-to-head comparative trials dedicated cardiovascular or renal outcome trials, or large globally diverse datasets are yet available; therefore, the current evidence should be interpreted as a clinical pharmacology synthesis rather than a comparative positioning claim.

articles.title: A pharmacokinetic study comparing a low-dose estrogen contraceptive transdermal system with an oral contraceptive tablet in healthy adult females.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the pharmacokinetics (PK) of a once-weekly low-dose estrogen contraceptive transdermal system (TDS) and a once-daily combined oral contraceptive (COC) in healthy women. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this Phase 1 study, 24 healthy women aged 18-35 years were randomized to a crossover sequence of three consecutive 168-h applications of the norelgestromin (NGMN; drug load, 4.86 mg)/ethinyl estradiol (EE; drug load, 0.264 mg) TDS to the abdomen (Treatment A) or buttock (Treatment B), followed by once-daily COC (drug load 0.18 mg norgestimate/0.025 mg EE) for 7 days (Treatment C). Plasma NGMN and EE concentrations were assessed using PK parameters. Application-site irritation, residual patch analysis, and safety were also evaluated. RESULTS: Variability in NGMN and EE exposure was lower for Treatments A and B versus Treatment C (AUCτ,ss: NGMN, 38.4% and 31.7% versus 47.0%; EE, 49.3% and 35.4% versus 51.2%) with comparable/lower Cp, ss(max) variability. EE Cp, ss(max). Normalized exposure were lower with the NGMN/EE TDS. No serious adverse events occurred. Residual patch analysis indicated delivery of ~200 µg/day NGMN and 19 µg/day EE. CONCLUSIONS: The NGMN/EE TDS demonstrated lower PK variability, EE peak concentrations and normalized EE exposure than the COC. No new safety signals were reported.

articles.title: Deficiency of Synaptotagmin 9 in the Hippocampal Region Induces Synaptic Damage and Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease Mice via BDNF/TrkB Signaling.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a prominent non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD) that severely affects patients' quality of life, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of hippocampal Synaptotagmin 9 (Syt9) in PD-related cognitive deficits. We found that Syt9 expression was significantly downregulated in the hippocampus of both MPTP-induced subacute PD mice and A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice, concomitant with cognitive impairment and synaptic damage. To determine causality, we performed hippocampal Syt9 knockdown and overexpression using AAV-mediated gene delivery. Syt9 knockdown exacerbated, while Syt9 overexpression alleviated, cognitive deficits and synaptic structural abnormalities in PD mice. Proteomic sequencing and pharmacological manipulations revealed that Syt9 may regulate the BDNF/TrkB signaling pathway at the protein level, likely by influencing BDNF vesicular transport, release, or stability. Intra-hippocampal BDNF supplementation rescued synaptic damage and cognitive impairment, whereas the TrkB antagonist ANA-12 reversed the protective effects of Syt9 overexpression. Collectively, our findings identify the Syt9/BDNF/TrkB axis as a key mechanism in PD-related cognitive impairment and suggest that targeting this pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for PD.

articles.title: Integrated extraction-detection platform based on Pt-Cu@PDA-rGO enzyme-free electrodes and porous microneedles for glucose monitoring.
articles.abstract: Enzyme-free electrochemical sensing avoids the stability issues and complex immobilization associated with natural enzymes. Here, a ternary Pt-Cu@PDA-rGO composite was prepared, in which polydopamine (PDA) reduces graphene oxide (GO) and anchors Pt-Cu alloy nanoparticles, suppressing agglomeration and enhancing electron transfer. The resulting electrode shows a linear response to glucose from 0.1 to 25 mM (R2 > 0.99), a sensitivity of 2.39 μA mM⁻1 cm⁻2, a detection limit of 0.21 mM, and storage stability over six weeks. A 15 × 15 porous poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) microneedle array was fabricated by micromolding, with a force of 0.17 N per needle at 300 μm displacement, sufficient for skin penetration. Applying 1.5 V reverse iontophoresis enhanced interstitial fluid (ISF) extraction, reaching 92.4 mg within 15 min. The microneedle array, reservoir chamber, Pt-Cu@PDA-rGO electrode, and a custom PCB were integrated into a single device. The extracted ISF is retained in the reservoir, where glucose is detected in situ. The signal is processed and transmitted via Bluetooth, and a universal port allows electrode replacement. In vivo studies in rats over 4.5 h and 12 h showed that the device tracked glucose fluctuations in agreement with a commercial glucometer, with a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) below 10% and all data points within zone A of the Clarke error grid. After 12 h of wear, TUNEL staining and IL-6 immunohistochemistry revealed no significant increase in apoptosis or inflammation. Overall, this integrated platform provides a minimally invasive and enzyme-free route to in situ glucose monitoring, showing promise for further development.

articles.title: Amorphous trehalose as a superior lyoprotectant for high-temperature long-term storage of freeze-dried mRNA-lipid nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: The large-scale global application of messenger ribonucleic acid-lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) is severely restricted by their mandatory ultra-low-temperature storage requirement, which poses critical logistics and transportation bottlenecks, especially in resource-limited regions. Lyophilization serves as a mild and well-established strategy to improve the thermal stability of biotherapeutics; nevertheless, complex physicochemical stresses during the lyophilization process may disrupt the structural integrity of mRNA and destroy the colloidal stability of LNP systems. Sucrose has been widely recognized as an efficient lyoprotectant, whereas the underlying mechanisms responsible for the stabilizing/destabilizing effects of crystalline and amorphous excipients remain incompletely understood. In this work, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were utilized to characterize lyophilized samples with diverse formulations. Combined with stability evaluation at 4 °C, 25 °C and 40 °C, the correlations between excipient crystallization behavior, thermodynamic properties and storage stability were systematically clarified. The results revealed that trehalose, with an intrinsically higher glass transition temperature in the amorphous state, exhibits superior lyoprotective capacity compared with sucrose under extreme storage conditions (40 °C), making it a more promising candidate for mRNA-LNP lyophilization.
