As a typical crystalline excipient, mannitol is inappropriate for single-component lyoprotectant application, as it severely impairs the long-term storage stability of mRNA-LNPs by damaging nanoparticle morphology and reducing nucleic acid encapsulation efficiency.

articles.title: Formulation and evaluation of tailored emulgels for enhanced topical cutaneous and ophthalmic delivery of antimicrobial and keratolytic agents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Topical drug delivery systems are increasingly favored for their ability to bypass first-pass metabolism and minimize systemic adverse effects. Emulgels, which combine the therapeutic benefits of emulsions and gels, offer a stable and effective platform for the delivery of both lipophilic and hydrophilic antimicrobial agents. The present study was designed to develop and optimize a versatile dual-route emulgel platform, featuring distinct formulations tailored for topical cutaneous delivery (incorporating salicylic acid for keratolytic and anti-acne applications) and topical ophthalmic delivery (incorporating ciprofloxacin and chloramphenicol for ocular surface infections), utilizing advanced statistical modeling to achieve superior therapeutic performance. METHODS: Emulgel formulations were prepared by integrating drug-loaded oil phases into aqueous gelling matrices, utilizing high-shear mixing to ensure homogeneity. Optimization of formulation variables, including polymer concentration and surfactant-to-co-surfactant ratios, was achieved using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on reduced polynomial models. The optimized formulations were evaluated for physical stability, rheological profile, globule size, and in vitro drug release kinetics across Cellophane® membranes. RESULTS: Statistical modeling identified ideal concentrations (1.25% gelling agent and 1:2 surfactant ratio) that yielded stable, nanostructured systems with globule sizes in the range of 185 to 210 nm. The formulations exhibited pseudoplastic, shear-thinning behavior, ensuring ease of application and structural stability over the study duration. In vitro release studies demonstrated sustained drug release profiles, with optimized batches showing significant permeability enhancement (Kp) and steady-state flux (Jss) compared to conventional topical preparations (p < 0.05 for all). Accelerated stability results over 90 days showed that the emulgels maintained their initial pH (5.6-6.1) and a smooth, white appearance. Quantitative assessment utilized similarity factors (f1 and f2), where f1 < 15 and f2 > 50 confirmed profile similarity after storage. The safety profile of the optimized emulgels evaluated via skin and eye irritation tests had no signs of erythema, edema, or clinical discomfort were observed during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: The study successfully developed stable, specialized emulgel formulations optimized for separate topical cutaneous and ophthalmic applications. The systematic integration of RSM enabled the precise formulation of delivery systems providing enhanced keratolytic, anti-acne, and anti-infective efficacy, supporting their potential application as robust alternatives to conventional vehicles in the management of localized dermal and ocular conditions.

articles.title: Zoledronic acid-loaded dissolvable microneedle patch for targeted regulation of osteoblast/osteoclast homeostasis as a potential treatment for peri-implantitis.
articles.abstract: Peri-implantitis is a major cause of dental implant failure, characterized by localized bone resorption driven by chronic inflammatory disruption of the balance between osteoblast and osteoclast activities, which ultimately leads to implant loosening and loss. Zoledronic acid (ZA) exerts potent inhibitory effects on osteoclasts and displays favorable bone-targeting properties; however, systemic administration of ZA carries a high risk of adverse reactions. To overcome this drawback, we fabricated hyaluronic acid-based dissolving microneedles loaded with zoledronic acid (ZA-DMNs) for local transmucosal delivery. This design aims to regulate the local osteoblast-osteoclast balance while eliminating systemic side effects to the greatest extent possible. The as-prepared ZA-DMNs possessed sufficient mechanical strength (withstanding a force of 0.15 N at half-height compression, exceeding the 0.1 N insertion threshold) and achieved a mucosal penetration depth of 140 μm, ensuring efficient transmucosal drug permeation. After insertion into mucosal tissue, the microneedle tips dissolved rapidly, releasing roughly 80% of the encapsulated ZA within 48 h. The liberated ZA binds tightly to bone surfaces with high affinity, locally suppressing osteoclast differentiation and bone resorptive activity. Furthermore, ZA-DMNs successfully rescued osteogenic function impaired by inflammatory microenvironments, and CCK-8 and live/dead staining assays confirmed their favorable biocompayibility. Taken together, these results preliminarily indicate that ZA-DMNs represent a promising local transmucosal delivery platform of ZA for the management of bone loss induced by peri-implantitis.

articles.title: A two-stage hybrid framework for predicting fine particle fraction from SEM images using deep feature extraction and class-specific regression.
articles.abstract: Fine particle fraction (FPF), a key predictor of inhalation powder efficacy, is conventionally measured using expensive, time-consuming in vitro methods that require specialized equipment. This study presents a novel approach for predicting FPF from scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images using deep learning and machine vision. The dataset comprised 764 preprocessed SEM images and their corresponding FPF values. A comparison of nine pretrained architectures identified DenseNet169 as the best feature extractor. A novel two-stage pipeline was then developed. In the first stage, the fine-tuned DenseNet169 model classified the images into four FPF classes. In the second stage, a random forest algorithm performed class-specific regression using the extracted feature vectors. The developed model predicted FPF with a weighted mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.84, representing an approximately 90% reduction in error compared with direct regression models, which produced errors of approximately 20. Statistical analysis indicated that the test set adequately represented the full dataset, and the model performed well on it. Grad-CAM heatmaps showed that the model focused on relevant regions of particle morphology. The proposed approach may facilitate rapid, cost-effective screening of inhalation formulations. By reducing material consumption, energy use, and laboratory waste, this method may also support industrial quality-control workflows and the development of dry powder inhalers.

articles.title: Effects of Sitagliptin Combined with GTS-21 on Improving Glycemic Control and Diabetic Nephropathy by Anti-Apoptosis in Leprdb/db Mice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Activation of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) by GTS-21 engages the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP). This study investigated adding GTS-21 to sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor used to increase endogenous GLP-1, confers additional benefit over sitagliptin monotherapy on glycemic control and diabetic nephropathy (DN) in Leprdb/db mice, focusing on anti-apoptotic mechanisms. METHODS: Leptin receptor-deficient (Leprdb/db, 8-week-old) mice were randomized into control (saline), sitagliptin (20 mg/kg), or combination (sitagliptin 20 mg/kg + GTS-21 4 mg/kg) groups for 4 weeks. Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), serum creatinine (Scr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and IL-6 were measured. Renal histology was evaluated by H&E staining. Apoptosis was assessed by TUNEL staining and cleaved caspase-3 expression. In vitro, HK-2 cells exposed to high glucose (30 mM) were treated with liraglutide (100 nM) and/or GTS-21 (20 nM) to examine apoptosis. RESULTS: Combination therapy significantly improved glucose tolerance at weeks 1 and 4 (AUC reduction, P=0.0366 and P=0.0435 vs control), whereas sitagliptin alone showed no effect. Both treatments reduced Scr (P=0.0002 for combination; P=0.0101 for monotherapy), but only combination therapy attenuated renal histological injury (P=0.002) and decreased IL-6 in serum and kidney (P=0.0433 and P=0.0041). Renal apoptosis was also suppressed, with reduced TUNEL-positive cells (P=0.0043) and cleaved caspase-3 (P=0.0122). In HK-2 cells, high glucose increased cleaved caspase-3 (P=0.0324), which was attenuated by liraglutide plus GTS-21 (P=0.0320). CONCLUSIONS: Add-on GTS-21 to sitagliptin improved glycemic control and attenuated diabetic nephropathy beyond sitagliptin monotherapy in Leprdb/db mice, with reduced renal inflammation and suppressed apoptosis. These findings suggest that combined activation of GLP-1 receptor and α7nAChR signaling warrants further investigation as a renoprotective strategy in diabetic nephropathy.

articles.title: Environmental enrichment preserves intestinal endocannabinoid signaling under LPS-inflammatory conditions.
articles.abstract: Environmental factors critically influence intestinal homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. The endocannabinoid system (ECS), a key regulator of immune, metabolic, and epithelial functions, has emerged as a promising pharmacological target in inflammatory disorders. However, whether environmental context influences intestinal ECS signaling and the coordinated mechanisms underlying intestinal homeostasis during inflammation remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of environmental enrichment (EE) on intestinal ECS regulation in the context of impaired intestinal homeostasis during lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced systemic inflammation. Adult male mice were housed under standard or enriched conditions for four weeks before LPS challenge (830 μg/kg, i.p., 24 h). ECS receptors (Cnr1, Cnr2), ECS-related targets (Trpv1, Pparγ), metabolic enzymes (Nape-pld, Dagl-β, Faah, Magl), inflammatory mediators (Tlr4, Tnf-α, Il-6), epithelial barrier markers (Ocln, Zo-1), endocannabinoid levels (AEA and 2-AG), selected bacterial taxa, and microbiota-derived metabolites were evaluated in the proximal colon. LPS induced coordinated changes in the intestinal ECS-related measures, endocannabinoid levels, inflammatory signaling, barrier-associated markers, and the selected microbial-metabolic profile. EE mitigated several of these changes, including ECS-related transcriptional and protein alterations and local inflammatory responses, while modulating tight-junction proteins, selected fecal bacterial taxa, microbiota-derived metabolites, and the integrated multivariate profile. Overall, EE modulates intestinal response profile consistent with greater resilience to inflammatory stress across ECS, inflammatory, barrier-associated, and microbial-metabolic measures. These findings suggest that ECS regulation may represent a context-dependent determinant of responsiveness to ECS-targeting pharmacological interventions.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Short-Chain Fatty Acids Mediate the Bone-Protective Effects of Metformin Against Postmenopausal Osteoporosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysbiosis-induced inflammation has been implicated in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP). Although metformin has shown benefits for bone health, the exact role of the gut microbiota in the mechanism underlying this relationship remains unclear. HYPOTHESIS/PURPOSE: We hypothesised that metformin could alleviate systemic inflammation in PMOP by augmenting the synthesis of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) by gut microbes. METHODS: Micro-computed tomography (μCT) was used to analyse the femurs. Faecal samples were collected for 16S rRNA sequencing and SCFAs detection. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and western blotting were used to detect mRNA and protein expression, respectively. Primary bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) were isolated to explore the effects of SCFAs on bone cell activity following inflammatory stimulation. RESULTS: Metformin improved trabecular bone microarchitecture in OVX mice, as shown by higher BV/TV, Tb.Th, and Tb.N, and reduced serum and tibial IL-1β and TNF-α. Metformin also increased the abundance of SCFA-producing genera, including Butyricimonas, Prevotella, Ruminococcus, Coprococcus, Oscillospira, and Sutterella, and elevated faecal propionate, butyrate, and valerate. Transplantation of metformin-adapted microbiota reproduced the bone-protective and anti-inflammatory effects, whereas GPR41/GPR43 deficiency abolished the benefits of metformin, propionate, and butyrate. In vitro, propionate and butyrate, but not valerate, promoted BMSC osteogenic differentiation and inhibited BMM-derived osteoclast differentiation under IL-1β/TNF-α-induced inflammation. CONCLUSIONS: Metformin modulates the gut microbiota by increasing propionate and butyrate synthesis, thereby reducing dysbiosis-induced inflammation and regulating BMSC and BMM differentiation to protect against PMOP.

articles.title: Tyramine modulates synaptic transmission in vertebrate neuromuscular junction by releasing catecholamines and activating alpha-adrenergic receptors.
articles.abstract: Tyramine is a biogenic amine whose role is closely linked to the sympathetic nervous system. Sympathetic axons densely innervate the neuromuscular junction regions of skeletal muscles. We hypothesized that tyramine might be the involvement in modulation of acetylcholine (ACh) release in the neuromuscular junctions. On the mouse Levator Auris Longus muscle it was found that tyramine enhances the loss of fluorescent false monoamine neurotransmitter FNN 511, preloaded into sympathetic varicosities located near the neuromuscular junctions. This indicates tyramine-induced release of endogenous catecholamines. Analysis of the ACh release demonstrated that tyramine decreases spontaneous exocytosis (estimated by the frequency of miniature endplate potentials) and evoked ACh secretion (assessed by the quantal content of the endplate potential). These inhibitory effects of tyramine were completely eliminated by doxazosin, an α1-adrenoreceptor blocker, but not SKF 86466, an α2-adrenoreceptor inhibitor. The negative action of tyramine on neuromuscular transmission was also manifested as a decrease in muscle contraction force during strong nerve activation. At the same time, tyramine did not inhibit the contractile responses to the direct muscle fiber stimulation. Finally, we obtained evidence of endogenous release of tyramine (and its derivative, octopamine) from the isolated neuromuscular preparation. Thus, tyramine can supress ACh release and, hence, contractile response to nerve activation probably by an indirect mechanism likely engaging the enhancement of endogenous catecholamine release and the downstream activation of α1-adrenoreceptors.

articles.title: The role of rapamycin in neural tube defects: insights from bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: Neural tube defects (NTDs) are the most severe congenital malformations of the central nervous system. Fetal developmental homeostasis disruptions heighten NTDs risk through aberrant maternal-fetal signaling and periconceptional medication exposure. Rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR signaling pathway, is a widely used clinical drug whose effects on embryonic neural development remain unclear. This study aimed to identify the potential drug targets for rapamycin in embryonic neural development. 18 rapamycin-NTDs targets were obtained by the network pharmacology approach. Functional enrichment analyses discovered they were associated with cell migration. AVPR2, CYP2C19, EPHB4, MMP9 and OXTR were identified as pivotal regulators mediating the effects of rapamycin on NTDs through machine learning. Immune infiltration analysis revealed the proportion of follicular helper T cells in the NTDs group was significantly lower and the pivotal genes were closely related with immune cell populations. Through single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, we identified 7 major cell types and confirmed the expression of rapamycin-NTDs key genes across them. Rapamycin-induced NTDs murine model displayed the NTDs incidence was 21.5% following 0.5mg/kg rapamycin exposure. Subsequent animal and cell experiments confirmed that MMP9 exhibited the strongest correlation in rapamycin-induced NTDs, which could regulate cell migration. Our results suggested that rapamycin may impair cell migration by suppressing MMP9, thereby contributing to the development of NTDs. These findings provide an experimental basis for elucidating the potential mechanisms of rapamycin in embryonic neural development. MMP9 might represent a target strategy for prevention and a potential biomarker for the early diagnosis of mTOR pathway abnormality or rapamycin-induced NTDs.

articles.title: Extracellular flux analysis and proteomic profiling indicate ibogaine promotes synaptic plasticity and neural repair by a metabolic preconditioning mechanism.
articles.abstract: We have examined how ibogaine may enhance synaptic plasticity and neural repair. Extracellular efflux analysis showed that ibogaine (3, 10 or 30 μM) produced a rapid (<5 minutes) and concentration-dependent suppression of mitochondrial function and glycolysis in mouse cortical neurons. Cell-based imaging demonstrated this metabolic inhibition was preceded by an elevation of the mitochondrial membrane potential and followed by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels. Like ibogaine, which blocks potassium channels, mitochondrial Kv1.3 channel (mitoKv1.3) inhibitors produce concordant changes over a similar timeframe. Following treatment with ibogaine (3, 10 or 30 μM) for 4 hours, a marked concentration-dependent rebound of energy production occurred 20 hours later suggestive of metabolic preconditioning. Indeed, proteomic profiling showed that oral ibogaine (100 mg/kg) administration to female mice produced changes in spinal cord protein abundance indicative of increasing metabolic stress from 0.25-24 hours that resolved by 72 hours. This was accompanied by activation, inhibition and reactivation of synaptic plasticity and neural repair signaling pathways at 0.25, 4-24 and 72 hours, respectively. Hence, by inducing transient metabolic stress, ibogaine may re-open a neurodevelopmental window characterized by enhanced synaptic plasticity and neural repair. Ibogaine binds with high affinity to the sigma-2 receptor. Like mitoKv1-3 inhibitors and sigma-2 receptor ligands, ibogaine transiently elevated AMP-activated protein kinase (0.25 hours) and temporally suppressed mechanistic target of rapamycin and lipid synthesis pathways (0.25-24 hours) implicated in enhanced synaptic plasticity and neural repair. These findings suggest ibogaine rewires and repairs neural circuits by a metabolic preconditioning mechanism, perhaps involving mitoKv1.3 and the sigma-2 receptor.

articles.title: Chrysin as a multi-target regulator of tramadol-induced testicular damage: Integration of inflammation, mitochondrial dynamics, and germ cell survival pathways.
articles.abstract: Tramadol, although commonly utilized as an analgesic, is an opioid derivative that may induce significant adverse consequences on the reproductive system. This study experimentally assessed the toxic effects of tramadol on testicular tissue and reproductive capabilities, as well as the protective capability of chrysin (CHR) against these effects. The results indicated that tramadol treatment caused considerable functional impairment in testicular tissue, as reflected by a notable reduction in sperm count, motility, and morphology, an elevation in the Cosentino score, and a decline in the Johnsen score and germinal epithelial thickness. Moreover, tramadol inhibited the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis by reducing testosterone, FSH, and LH levels. At the molecular level, tramadol induced heightened oxidative stress, inhibited antioxidant defense mechanisms, intensified the inflammatory response, and compromised mitochondrial function. Furthermore, an elevation in DNA damage indicators and a notable activation of the cellular stress response were observed. Substantial disturbances were also noted in miRNA expression patterns and the control of target genes. Nonetheless, CHR therapy predominantly ameliorated all functional, hormonal, and molecular alterations induced by tramadol. Spermatogenesis was partially reinstated, and sperm parameters together with hormone levels approached values comparable to those of the control groups. Moreover, substantial advancements were attained in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and DNA damage indicators. In conclusion, CHR has significant protective and regulatory actions against tramadol-induced testicular damage.

articles.title: Hyperthermia exacerbates methamphetamine cardiotoxicity by promoting neutrophil-dominant inflammation and Map3k6-associated p38/ERK signaling.
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine (METH) abuse is frequently accompanied by life-threatening hyperthermia, yet the contribution of hyperthermia to METH-induced cardiac injury remains poorly defined. Here, we tested whether elevated ambient temperature amplifies METH cardiotoxicity by aggravating hyperthermia. C57BL/6 mice were exposed to different ambient temperatures (18 °C, 22 °C, or 28 °C) and treated with METH. METH rapidly increased core body temperature, whereas exposure at 28 °C further intensified hyperthermia and caused 20% mortality. In surviving mice, METH at 28 °C significantly reduced cardiac function-including heart rate, cardiac output, stroke volume, ejection fraction and fractional shortening, and induced myocardial eosinophilic degeneration, focal myofiber disruption, cardiomyocyte lysis and inflammatory cell infiltration. Cardiac transcriptomics revealed a distinct inflammatory program enriched for cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, chemokine signaling, leukocyte chemotaxis and neutrophil migration. RT-qPCR confirmed increased cardiac expression of CCL2, CXCL1, ITGAM, ICAM-1 and MMP9, and inflammatory cytokines were also elevated. Immune-infiltration analysis identified prominent neutrophil accumulation, and gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) indicated activation of oxidative stress-related pathways. Among stress-related kinases, mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 6 (Map3k6, also known as ASK2) was upregulated and positively correlated with neutrophil-dominant infiltration and inflammatory markers. METH at 28 °C also increased p38 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) phosphorylation. These findings identify elevated ambient temperature as a critical amplifier of METH-induced cardiac injury and implicate Map3k6-associated p38/ERK activation in hyperthermia-associated cardiac inflammation and functional impairment. Collectively, our results indicate that hyperthermia exacerbates METH cardiotoxicity, potentially involving Map3k6-associated p38/ERK signaling and neutrophil-dominant immune infiltration, providing new mechanistic insights into temperature-associated cardiac vulnerability following METH abuse.

articles.title: High Normal dietary casein attenuates bisphenol A-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats: Preservation of renal integrity, glucose homeostasis, and immune surveillance via modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) causes multiorgan toxicity via oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and the effect of nutritionally relevant elevation of casein intake is unknown. To evaluate whether a nutritionally relevant elevation of dietary casein (18% vs. 14%) attenuates BPA-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats, male Wistar rats were divided into four groups (n = 8/group) and treated for 35 days: control (14% casein), casein 18% alone, BPA (50 mg/kg/day +14% casein), and BPA + 18% casein. We measured oxidative and inflammatory markers, renal function, metabolic parameters, hematological parameters, histopathology and immunohistochemistry in kidney, spleen, and pancreas. BPA significantly increased malondialdehyde, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, creatinine, kidney injury molecule-1, insulin resistance, white blood cells, neutrophils, and monocytes, and decreased reduced glutathione, glutathione S-transferase, superoxide dismutase, catalase, interleukin-4, serum soluble CD4 and CD8 protein levels, hemoglobin, red blood cells, platelets, and lymphocytes. BPA also caused renal tubular necrosis, splenic degeneration, pancreatic fibrosis, and upregulated caspase-3 and inducible nitric oxide synthase. Co-administration of 18% casein partially attenuated these effects, reducing malondialdehyde by 35-40%, creatinine by 40%, and insulin resistance by 53%, and restoring antioxidant enzymes and glucose tolerance. However, several parameters remained significantly different from controls. Nutritionally relevant elevation of casein (18%) provides significant partial protection against BPA-induced toxicity, supporting dietary protein modulation as a supportive strategy.

articles.title: Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide induces osteoblast senescence and defective mineralization associated with indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1-kynurenine-aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling.
articles.abstract: AIM: To determine whether Porphyromonas gingivalis-derived lipopolysaccharide (P.g-LPS) is associated with osteoblast senescence and defective mineralization involving inflammation-related indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1)-kynurenine (Kyn)-aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathway and to examine its upstream regulation. METHODS: hFOB1.19 human osteoblasts and zebrafish were exposed to P.g-LPS. Osteogenic differentiation, senescence, IDO1/Kyn/AhR signaling, Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)/RELA regulation, and rescue by the IDO1 inhibitor epacadostat or AhR inhibitor CH223191 were assessed using staining, qPCR, western blotting, ELISA, gene silencing, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS: P.g-LPS reduced osteogenic differentiation and mineralization and increased senescence-associated markers in hFOB1.19 cells and zebrafish. P.g-LPS increased IDO1 expression and Kyn levels; epacadostat attenuated osteogenic impairment and senescence-associated changes. Exogenous Kyn increased AhR-responsive gene expression and produced similar phenotypes, which were attenuated by CH223191. TLR4 knockdown reduced P.g-LPS-induced IDO1, NFKB1, and RELA expression, and RELA overexpression enhanced wild-type IDO1 promoter activity, with loss of this response after mutation of the predicted NF-κB site. CONCLUSION: P.g-LPS-induced osteogenic impairment and senescence-associated changes involve IDO1-Kyn-AhR-related signaling, alongside TLR4-associated responses and RELA-dependent IDO1 promoter activity. Inhibition of IDO1 or AhR attenuated these phenotypes in the experimental models.

articles.title: Discovery of the mechanism of Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction in the treatment of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy with Qi Deficiency and Blood Stasis based on the dynamic metabolic trajectory analysis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction (HGWD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has shown clinical efficacy in the treatment of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) with Qi deficiency and blood stasis syndrome. However, its pharmacodynamic material basis and underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to systematically elucidate the pharmacodynamic material basis and therapeutic mechanisms of HGWD in the treatment of DPN using an integrated Chinmedomics strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A rat model of DPN with Qi deficiency and blood stasis syndrome was established by streptozotocin (STZ) injection combined with dietary intervention and exhaustive swimming. HGWD was administered continuously for 8 weeks to assess its therapeutic effects. In addition to conventional pharmacological assessments, ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis (ASCA) was applied to urinary metabolomics analysis to dynamically track metabolic trajectories and characterize time-dependent changes in disease-related urinary biomarkers. Blood-absorbed components in the HGWD-treated group were characterized using UHPLC-QE-Orbitrap-MS. Correlation analysis was then performed among urinary biomarkers, key pharmacodynamic indicators, and in vivo active components. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro experiments were further conducted to validate the core active components and their corresponding targets. RESULTS: HGWD significantly improved neurological function and alleviated pathological damage in the DPN rat model. Urinary metabolomics analysis identified 28 disease-related urinary biomarkers that were markedly modulated by HGWD treatment. Under conditions of confirmed therapeutic efficacy, 98 blood-absorbed components, including 63 prototype compounds and 35 metabolites, were identified. Integrated correlation analysis and network pharmacology revealed eight key pharmacodynamic components and three core targets closely associated with the therapeutic effects of HGWD. Among these components, astragaloside II, paeoniflorin, and quercetin were identified as major bioactive compounds, which may exert therapeutic effects by regulating the protein expression of P-gp, PTP1B, and MMP2. CONCLUSION: This study systematically clarified the pharmacodynamic material basis and therapeutic mechanisms of HGWD in the treatment of DPN using an integrated Chinmedomics approach. The integrated analysis identified 17 urinary biomarkers, 8 core components, and 3 core targets, namely ABCB1, MMP2, and PTPN1, which were further supported by molecular simulations and in vitro validation These findings provide a comprehensive strategy for deciphering the mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine formulas and support the potential application of HGWD in DPN treatment.

articles.title: Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides ameliorate inflammation and lipid accumulation in T2DM-induced MASLD via miR-155-regulated PPARγ signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Agriophyllum squarrosum (L.) Moq., is a traditional medicinal herb first recorded in the "Four Medical Tantras" during the 8th century AD. It is commonly employed in Mongolian medicine for various therapeutic diseases, including the dispelling epidemics, heat clearance, detoxification, and diuresis. This herb is known to inhibit "He Yi," regulate "Ba Da Gan," and is utilized in the treatment of "Xi He Ri Xi Jing Bing" which corresponds to modern diabetes and xiaoke in traditional Chinese medicine. Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides (AOS) are recognized as major bioactive constituents, however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)-related metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigates the therapeutic effects of AOS in T2DM-MASLD and explores the underlying mechanisms involving miR-155-mediated signaling pathways. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In vivo, db/db mice were treated with AOS, and hepatic lipid accumulation and insulin resistance were evaluated using biochemical and histological analyses. Hepatic expression of miR-155 and associated signaling proteins was observed by qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Exosomes derived from ATMs of db/db mice were co-cultured with AML-12 hepatocytes to investigate the role of exosomal miR-155 in MASLD progression. In vitro, inflammatory cytokine production and miR-155 expression were quantified using ELISA and qRT-PCR, while exosomal miR-155 secretion was evaluated in glucolipid-induced cellular injury models. RESULTS: AOS treatment reduced hepatic steatosis and improved insulin resistance in db/db mice. AOS was associated with decreased hepatic miR-155 expression. Exosomal miR-155 derived from ATMs aggravated hepatocyte injury in the co-culture system, accompanied by increased expression of SREBP1c, NLRP3, and NF-κB p65. In vitro, AOS inhibited exosomal miR-155 secretion and downregulated the expression of SREBP1c, P2X7R, NF-κB p65, and inhibitor of IκBα, thus attenuating glucolipid metabolism-associated inflammatory responses and lipid dysregulation. CONCLUSION: AOS ameliorates inflammation, hepatic lipid accumulation, and insulin resistance in T2DM-associated MASLD, possibly via suppression of miR-155 and modulation of downstream inflammatory and lipogenic signaling pathways. These results identify AOS as a promising therapeutic candidate for treating T2DM-associated MASLD.

articles.title: Locomotor stimulant and methamphetamine-like interoceptive effects of putative impurity N-ethyl-methamphetamine in rodents: Role of Phase I metabolism.
articles.abstract: Over the past 20 years, N-ethyl-methamphetamine (NEM) has been identified in seized methamphetamine (METH) samples. Often considered a byproduct or impurity of illicit METH synthesis, its structural similarity to METH suggests that it may have pharmacological actions of its own or be metabolically converted to METH or amphetamine (AMPH) in vivo. These studies assessed the potency and effectiveness of NEM as a locomotor stimulant compared to METH in NIH Swiss mice, and probed the role of cytochrome P450 (CYP) vs non-CYP metabolism in these locomotor effects using pretreatments with the broad spectrum CYP inhibitor 1-aminobenzotriazole (1-ABT) or the selective CYP2D6 inhibitor quinidine. Blood samples taken from mice treated with NEM, with and without pretreatments of 1-ABT or quinidine, were quantitively analyzed for NEM, METH, and AMPH using Quadrupole Time-of-Flight. Additionally, the discriminative stimulus effects of NEM were assayed in Sprague-Dawley rats trained to discriminate METH from saline. NEM produced dose-dependent locomotor stimulant and METH-like interoceptive effects, but with a slower onset and less potently than METH. Locomotor stimulant effects of NEM were abolished by pretreatment with 1-ABT or quinidine, and both pretreatments also decreased conversion of NEM to METH and AMPH in mouse blood. These data demonstrate METH-like biological effects of NEM and suggest that the likely mechanism for these effects is metabolic conversion of NEM to METH and AMPH via CYP2D6. NEM thus functions as a prodrug for METH and AMPH, and would be expected to have METH-like abuse liability in humans. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: N-ethyl-methamphetamine (NEM) has been identified in seized methamphetamine (METH) samples, and is typically considered a byproduct or impurity of illicit METH synthesis. These studies demonstrate METH-like biological effects of NEM and suggest that the likely mechanism for these effects is metabolic conversion of NEM to METH and AMPH via CYP2D6. NEM thus functions as a prodrug for METH and AMPH, and would be expected to have METH-like abuse liability in humans.

articles.title: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 is involved in the microtubule-mediated regulation of intraocular pressure.
articles.abstract: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is known as the most common gene responsible for familial Parkinson disease (PD). This protein plays a key role in the neurodegenerative pathways associated with PD. LRRK2 also plays critical roles in actin dynamics and microtubule cytoskeletal assembly in the cells. In addition to PD, actin and microtubule cytoskeletons are associated with the onset and development of glaucoma by regulating the intraocular pressure (IOP) in humans and animals. However, the role of LRRK2 in regulating IOP remains unclear. Hence, this study investigated the contribution of LRRK2 to cytoskeleton-mediated regulation of IOP. LRRK2 was detected in primary human trabecular meshwork cells by immunofluorescence and western blotting analysis. Inhibition of the function and the expression of LRRK2 by LRRK2 inhibitors and LRRK2 siRNA, induced a significant reduction of TEER in these cells. TEER reduction by an LRRK2 inhibitor was attenuated by paclitaxel, a-tubulin polymerization inducer, but not by jasplakinolide, an actin polymerization inducer, suggesting that inhibition of LRRK2 induced depolymerization of microtubules, resulting in decreased TEER. Finally, LRRK2 gene knockout and LRRK2 inhibition led to a significant reduction of IOP in C57BL6J mice and Japanese white rabbits, respectively. These results suggested that LRRK2 is associated with catalysis of a-tubulin in trabecular meshwork cells and regulates IOP in mice and rabbits. Hence, there is a possibility that an LRRK2 inhibitor contributes to glaucoma therapeutics. Further evaluation to clarify the role of LRRK2 in IOP regulation is needed. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: In this study, a significant contribution of LRRK2 to the regulation of intraocular pressure (IOP) was shown. Inhibition of LRRK2 results in a decrease in TEER of the trabecular meshwork cells, associated with the depolymerization of microtubules. Furthermore, both LRRK2 knockout and administration of the LRRK2 inhibitor induced a significant decrease in the IOP in animals. These results clearly indicate the role of LRRK2 in the regulation of IOP and the possibility of a novel therapeutic approach to glaucoma.

articles.title: Antinociceptive interaction of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol and cannabidiol in a humanized mouse model of sickle cell disease.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is characterized by recurrent, debilitating pain. Opioid analgesics are routinely used in its management, but limited efficacy and pervasive side effects prompt many patients with SCD to seek alternatives, including cannabis. Prior work has shown that 2 major cannabis constituents, Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), exert antinociceptive effects in HbSS-BERK mice, a model of SCD. The present study investigated the pharmacological interaction between these 2 agents and characterized the effects associated with repeated coadministration. Fixed-ratio isobolographic analyses demonstrated that Δ9-THC and CBD produced dose-dependent antinociception following acute coadministration. Fixed-ratio isobolographic analyses showed that the experimentally determined median effective dose of the mixture was lower than the theoretical additive dose, but the difference was not statistically significant, supporting an additive antinociceptive interaction. Repeated coadministration maintained antinociceptive efficacy over 14 days and reduced SCD-evoked anxiety-like behavior in one cohort but did not improve recognition-memory deficits. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analyses revealed that repeated coadministration increased plasma CBD concentrations, produced a modest increase in Δ9-THC exposure, and markedly elevated circulating levels of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycerol. Molecular analyses of spinal cord tissue showed that HbSS-BERK mice exhibited increased oxidative stress (malondialdehyde, MDA) and proinflammatory signaling (interleukin [IL]-1β mRNA), with no change in anti-inflammatory signaling (IL-10 mRNA). Following 14 days of treatment, CBD reduced MDA and IL-1β transcription, whereas Δ9-THC reduced MDA and increased IL-10. Notably, the combination treatment simultaneously reduced oxidative stress, suppressed IL-1β, and enhanced IL-10. Together, these findings demonstrate an additive antinociceptive interaction between Δ9-THC and CBD and sustained efficacy during repeated administration in SCD mice. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Chronic pain in sickle cell disease remains difficult to treat, and many patients use cannabis despite limited understanding of how its constituents interact to produce analgesia. This study demonstrates that the 2 major phytocannabinoids in cannabis, Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol and cannabidiol, produce additive antinociceptive effects in a humanized mouse model of sickle cell disease, and their combined efficacy is maintained during repeated administration without detectable tolerance.

articles.title: Design and optimization of naringenin-loaded organogels for topical management of bacterial infections.
articles.abstract: Bacterial skin infections are increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance, and naringenin, a citrus flavanone with membrane disrupting antibacterial activity, is limited in topical use by poor aqueous solubility and low dermal penetration. The present work was undertaken to develop and optimize naringenin loaded organogels for topical antibacterial application using a systematic quality by design approach. Naringenin loaded organogels were prepared by the hot emulsification technique and optimized through a 32 full factorial design in which glyceryl monostearate (10 to 20% w/w) and Capryol™ PGMC (5 to 15% w/w) concentrations were varied. The formulations were characterized for gel strength, viscosity, spreadability, drug content, drug excipient compatibility by FTIR, in vitro drug release, release kinetics, antibacterial activity and accelerated stability. The pH values (6.12 to 6.42) were suitable for topical application and the drug content was high (96.8 to 99.1%). Gel strength (42.6 to 92.2 g) and viscosity (3842.6 to 9922.3 cps) increased with glyceryl monostearate concentration, whereas spreadability (16.5 to 29.6 g · cm/s) decreased. Response surface methodology identified MF5, containing 15% w/w glyceryl monostearate and 10% w/w Capryol™ PGMC, as the optimized formulation, with experimental values for gel strength (78.5 g), viscosity (6082.4 cps) and drug release at 12 h (89.74%) closely matching the predicted values (relative error below 2.5%). The optimized formulation followed zero order release kinetics (R2 = 0.9859) with a non Fickian diffusion mechanism (n = 0.79), retained antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, and remained stable under accelerated conditions for three months. Optimized naringenin loaded organogel exhibited favorable physiochemical properties with an sustained in-vitro drug release and antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. The optimized formulation showed reduced antibacterial activity under the same experimental conditions when compared with the standard ciprofloxacin, and showed to release the antibiotic continuously from the organogel matrix. By using the factorial design approach, an optimized formulation having reproducible quality attributes and acceptable physicochemical stability after accelerated storage was achieved.

articles.title: Amantadine attenuates LPS-associated acute hepatic injury through anti-inflammatory and antiapoptotic responses: potential involvement of TXNIP/NLRP3-related signaling.
articles.abstract: The hepatoprotective potential of amantadine (AMN) against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-triggered hepatic injury was investigated by evaluating inflammation, inflammasome activation, and apoptosis-related signaling pathways. The study consists of four groups: Control, LPS, LPS + AMN, and AMN. Histopathological changes were evaluated in hematoxylin and eosin-stained liver sections. Immunohistochemical analyses were performed to assess C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) activities were measured as biochemical indicators of liver injury. Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), interleukin-18 (IL-18), NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3), thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP), and Bcl-2-associated X protein (BAX) gene expression was determined liver tissue. LPS administration caused severe histopathological damage, inflammatory cell infiltration, and significant elevations in AST and ALT activities. Increased immunoreactivity of CRP, SAA, and TNF-α, together with upregulated IL-1β, IL-18, NLRP3, TXNIP, and BAX expression, indicated enhanced inflammatory and apoptotic responses. Administration of AMN was associated with attenuation of tissue damage, accompanied by lower inflammatory marker levels, decreased serum transaminase activities, and altered expression of key genes related to inflammasome activation and apoptotic pathways. No significant differences were detected between the LPS + AMN groups and controls groups. The present findings are consistent with an association between AMN administration and attenuation of LPS-associated hepatic injury, accompanied by changes in inflammatory responses, inflammasome-related signaling, and apoptosis-related pathways. These findings are consistent with a potential hepatoprotective effect of AMN in inflammation-associated liver injury and warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Bacillus-based probiotics ameliorate bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in rats: coupling intestinal barrier reinforcement to the modulation of M2 macrophage polarization/TGF-β/p38MAPK and inflammasome-driven pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic, progressive lung disorder with an 87.5% mortality rate recorded in aged patients. Emerging evidence bridges gut dysbiosis to PF pathogenesis. The consumption of a Bacillus-based probiotic exhibited immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects by alleviating gut dysbiosis and restoring gut microbiome composition, positioning it as a promising therapeutic strategy for gut-organ axis disorders. The present study investigated the therapeutic effects of Bacillus-based probiotics in a rat model of PF by targeting the gut-lung axis. Rats were randomly assigned to five groups: Group I (the normal control group) and Group II received a single intratracheal instillation of bleomycin (BLM) (5 mg/kg). All treated groups received BLM and commenced treatment fourteen days later. Group III: received B. clausii. Group IV: received B. coagulans. Group V: received a combination of both strains. In vitro and in vivo analyses showed that the probiotic strains exhibited gut survivability, colonization associated with restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, and an SCFA profile. The dual therapy exerted a notable immunomodulatory effect by suppressing pulmonary M2 macrophage polarization (CD206 and Arg1), inhibiting the TGF-β/p38MAPK-JNK/NF-κB signaling cascade, mitigating inflammatory and fibrotic responses, and diminishing NLRP3/Caspase-1/IL-1β/GSDMD-N-mediated pyroptosis, thereby disrupting the vicious cycle of inflammation and fibrogenesis. Interplay with the Nrf2 axis activates antioxidant defense. This study resolves this knowledge gap by investigating the therapeutic potential of Bacillus-based probiotics to alleviate PF by modulating the gut-lung axis, offering an innovative platform for the treatment of PF that extends beyond current Lactobacillus-focused research.

articles.title: Exploring the addictive potential of α-methylfentanyl and acetyl-α-methylfentanyl in animal models.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The abuse profiles of α-methylfentanyl and acetyl-α-methylfentanyl remain poorly characterized in preclinical models. This study systematically evaluated their addiction-related behaviours and underlying pharmacological features. METHODS: Conditioned place preference (CPP) was tested in mice with gradient doses of fentanyl, α-methylfentanyl and acetyl-α-methylfentanyl. Intravenous self-administration, behavioural economic demand curves, cue- and drug-primed reinstatement, and drug discrimination assays were conducted in rats. ED₅₀ values were calculated and compared across compounds. RESULTS: All three compounds induced significant CPP, with acetyl-α-methylfentanyl showing ~ 30-fold lower potency. In self-administration, all compounds produced inverted U-shaped dose-response curves, with peak infusion rates at 0.5 µg/kg/infusion. Fentanyl exhibited the highest essential value (EV) in demand curve analysis, indicating stronger reinforcing efficacy. A single naloxone pretreatment significantly attenuated both cue- and drug-primed reinstatement. Drug discrimination ED₅₀ was 11.06, 12.65 and 128.3 µg/kg for fentanyl, α-methylfentanyl and acetyl-α-methylfentanyl, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: α-methyl substitution selectively reduces reinforcing efficacy without altering reward perception; acetylation attenuates both reward and discriminative stimulus effects while preserving reinforcing capacity. µ-Opioid receptor signalling mediates relapse-like behaviour, supporting long-acting antagonists as potential interventions.

articles.title: Protective effects of cannabidiol against acute stress: behavioral responses and corticosterone concentrations in female Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cannabidiol (CBD) has been widely investigated for its potential anxiolytic and stress-modulating effects. This study evaluated whether CBD reduces the stress response induced by acute restraint stress in rats. METHODS: Thirty-six female Wistar rats were randomly assigned to six groups. Four experimental groups received CBD at different doses (2, 10, 20, and 100 mg/kg), while two control groups received the placebo (CBD vehicle medium-chain triglycerides). Sixty minutes after administration, the animals treated with CBD and one placebo-treated group (stressed control group) were subjected to 60 min of restraint stress. The other placebo-treated group (nonstressed control group) was not subjected to restraint stress. Subsequently, all animals were tested in the open field (OF) for 30 min. Immediately after the OF test, blood samples were collected for corticosterone analysis. Plasma corticosterone concentrations were determined using a commercial ELISA kit. RESULTS: In the OF, distance traveled differed significantly between groups, although no significant differences were observed among the different CBD doses. Compared with stressed control rats, CBD-treated rats spent more time in the center of the OF arena, suggesting reduced anxiety-like behavior. Plasma corticosterone concentrations did not differ significantly between groups. At 90 min after the onset of stress (30 min after the end of restraint stress), corticosterone concentrations did not differ between CBD-treated and untreated rats. CONCLUSION: CBD showed no effect on locomotor activity but increased center time, suggesting anxiolytic-like effects. Further studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Pimpinella brachycarpa extract attenuates periodontal inflammation by modulating the PI3K/Akt-NF-κB signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study was conducted to investigate the preventive effects of Pimpinella brachycarpa extract (PBE), which has demonstrated anti-inflammatory effects but whose molecular mechanisms and active components are not completely understood, in experimental periodontitis and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms. METHODS: The protective effects of PBE were evaluated in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced periodontitis rat model by assessing histological changes, TRAP-positive osteoclast presence, and alveolar bone loss. Network pharmacology, protein-protein interaction network analysis, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and molecular docking were performed to predict the potential targets and mechanisms of PBE. The anti-inflammatory effects of PBE were further investigated in RAW264.7 macrophages and human periodontal ligament fibroblasts (PDLFs). Inflammatory mediators, cytokines, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and PI3K/Akt/NF-κB signaling-related proteins were analyzed. Major constituents of PBE were identified using UPLC-QTOF-MS, and their anti-inflammatory activities were evaluated in vitro. RESULTS: PBE attenuated periodontal tissue destruction in LPS-induced periodontitis rats, as demonstrated by reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, decreased CEJ-ABC distance, and suppression of TRAP-positive osteoclast presence. Network pharmacology analysis identified the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway as a key target associated with the anti-inflammatory effects of PBE. In RAW264.7 macrophages, PBE significantly reduced the production of NO, PGE2, TNF-α, and IL-1β. In PDLFs, PBE suppressed IL-1β-induced production of PGE2, IL-6, and IL-1β and downregulated the expression of MMP-3, MMP-8, and MMP-13. Furthermore, PBE inhibited the phosphorylation of PI3K, Akt, IKK, IκBα, and NF-κB p65. Chemical profiling identified chlorogenic acid, luteolin 7-O-glucuronide, apigenin 7-O-glucuronide, and luteolin 3'-O-glucuronide as major constituents. Among these, flavonoid glucuronides exhibited stronger anti-inflammatory activities than chlorogenic acid in vitro. CONCLUSION: The present findings indicate that PBE exerts anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective effects in experimental models of periodontitis. The observed effects were associated with suppression of PI3K/Akt-NF-κB signaling. In addition, flavonoid glucuronides identified in PBE exhibited anti-inflammatory activities in vitro. Further studies are required to clarify the contribution of individual constituents to the biological activity of PBE.

articles.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
articles.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 ×  reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR,   KRAS G 12 C    , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90  per condition; all p > 0.20  ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

articles.title: Indication-specific adverse event profiles of semaglutide and liraglutide: a FAERS disproportionality analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: By 2021, regulatory agencies had approved two glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), semaglutide and liraglutide, for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Since then, concerns have emerged about whether adverse events (AEs) differ by GLP-1RA or indication. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports (2021-2025) to compare adverse events associated with semaglutide and liraglutide indications. Comparisons with metformin and orlistat helped distinguish drug-related signals from disease-related signals. We defined safety signals by a positive reporting odds ratio and at least one other positive disproportionality metric. RESULTS: Among 8,213,105 FAERS reports, 33,259 met the inclusion criteria. Semaglutide generated more reports for type 2 diabetes than for obesity (13,168 vs. 5,444), and liraglutide showed a similar pattern (1,201 vs. 837). GLP-1RAs exhibited gastrointestinal AEs. Semaglutide showed signals for slowed gastrointestinal motility across both indications, particularly impaired gastric emptying, in both type 2 diabetes and obesity reports (ROR = 8.35, 95% CI = 1.16-59.97 and ROR = 4.01, 95% CI = 2.12-7.58, respectively). Liraglutide demonstrated signals for more severe gastrointestinal AEs, including abdominal distention in type 2 diabetes (ROR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.12-1.91) and pancreatitis in obesity (ROR = 2.90, 95% CI = 1.91-4.39) reports. Additional notable safety signals included optic ischemic neuropathy with semaglutide (ROR = 4.42, 95% CI = 1.41-13.87) and psychiatric AEs, including suicidal ideation (ROR = 5.98, 95% CI = 1.24-24.19). CONCLUSION: We identified robust signals for GLP-1RAs, including impaired gastric emptying, ileus, and ischemic optic neuropathy. Additionally, we identified signals for suicidal ideation. Future studies are needed to evaluate for causal relationships.

articles.title: Comparative performance of multiple predictive models constructed for budesonide nebulized formulation requirements.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Developing rational demand forecasting plans for National Centralized Volume-Based Procurement (NCVBP) pharmaceuticals is critical to ensuring patient access while avoiding drug inventory surplus, thereby facilitating refined hospital management and reducing operational costs. This study therefore compared the predictive performance of multiple models to identify an optimal approach for forecasting hospital demand for budesonide nebulized formulation. METHODS: Using 48 months of actual utilization data (2022-2025) for budesonide nebulized formulation, a fifth-batch NCVBP product, we systematically evaluated the forecasting performance of 10 single models, 3 hybrid models, and 1 weighted ensemble model. RESULTS: On the pediatric hospital dataset, the TBATS-XGB hybrid model achieved the best performance on the test set, yielding the lowest mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 12.43%, along with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 5486.0 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3659.8. CONCLUSION: The TBATS-XGB hybrid model can serve as a valuable reference for NCVBP drug quantity forecasting, addressing the limitations of conventional empirical estimation methods that often fail to capture structural changes and seasonal fluctuations in demand. Moreover, because it requires only historical usage data for deployment, this approach may be highly generalizable to hospital settings with limited data infrastructure.

articles.title: Gastrodin alleviates mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease via candidate targeting of ACHE, S1PR5, SERPINE1, and TOP2A: an integrative computational and cellular study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and its prodromal mild cognitive impairment (MCI) lack effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies. Gastrodin (GAS), the major bioactive compound of Gastrodia elata, exhibits pronounced neuroprotective effects. However, the precise candidate molecular targets and systematic mechanisms by which GAS protects against AD and MCI remain poorly clarified; target engagement is inferred from computational simulation rather than direct biochemical validation. METHODS/RESULTS: This study adopted an integrated approach of network pharmacology, transcriptome-based machine learning, molecular simulation, and in vitro cellular validation to explore the therapeutic mechanisms of GAS against AD/MCI. A total of 127 overlapping therapeutic targets of GAS, AD, and MCI were identified, which were mainly enriched in synaptic transmission and calcium signaling pathways. Four core hub genes (ACHE, S1PR5, SERPINE1, and TOP2A) were further screened by intersecting candidate targets with AD differentially expressed genes from the GSE329677 dataset. The ensemble Logistic + SVM machine learning model exhibited optimal diagnostic efficiency with an AUC value of 0.897. Molecular docking and 50 ns molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that GAS stably bound to the four target proteins and maintained stable binding states under physiological conditions. In an Aβ1-42 oligomer-injured N2a neuronal model, GAS showed no significant cytotoxicity at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 μM. Notably, 25 μM GAS markedly reversed Aβ1-42-induced neuronal death and excessive intracellular ROS accumulation. CONCLUSION: This study identifies four novel candidate core therapeutic targets of GAS against AD/MCI and provides computational evidence for their stable atomic-level binding characteristics. GAS exerts prominent neuroprotective effects through anti-apoptotic and antioxidant mechanisms in Aβ-injured neurons. These findings provide a novel theoretical basis and preclinical evidence for the development of GAS as a natural candidate agent for AD intervention.

articles.title: Development and validation of machine learning models for predicting pancreatic injury observed after tigecycline initiation: a retrospective real-world study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tigecycline is widely used for severe infections and infections caused by multidrug-resistant pathogens. Although pancreatic injury observed after tigecycline initiation is relatively uncommon, it may adversely affect patient prognosis. Currently, clinical management mainly relies on post-treatment monitoring, and reliable tools for early risk prediction are lacking. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting pancreatic injury observed after tigecycline initiation using real-world clinical data. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients who received tigecycline for at least 3 consecutive days at Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, between January 2020 and March 2024. The primary outcome was pancreatic injury observed after tigecycline initiation, defined as serum amylase >405U/L and/or serum lipase >180 U/L within 7 days after tigecycline initiation. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, concomitant medications, tigecycline treatment information, and baseline laboratory parameters were collected. Missing values were imputed using K-nearest neighbors imputation, and class imbalance was addressed using SMOTE. The dataset was randomly divided into training and test sets at an 8:2 ratio. Eight machine learning algorithms were developed and compared. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value and F1 score. SHAP analysis was used for model interpretation. RESULTS: A total of 623 patients were included, of whom 146 (23.4%) developed pancreatic injury. Among the evaluated algorithms, LightGBM had the highest point-estimate AUC. The final 7-feature LightGBM model achieved an AUC of 0.726, accuracy of 0.728, sensitivity of 0.379, specificity of 0.833, PPV of 0.407, NPV of 0.816, and F1 score of 0.393 on the held-out test set. These results indicate moderate discrimination but limited sensitivity. CONCLUSION: With relatively high specificity and negative predictive value, this model may provide preliminary risk stratification information and assist targeted pancreatic enzyme monitoring during tigecycline therapy, particularly for identifying patients at lower predicted risk. However, prospective external validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Patterns and appropriateness of antipsychotic prescribing in community-dwelling older adults: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antipsychotics carry substantial risk in older adults, yet their use among community-dwelling outpatients remains insufficiently characterized in Saudi Arabia, where most prior work examined potentially inappropriate medications broadly or within psychiatric services. This study assessed patterns and appropriateness of antipsychotic prescribing and examined factors associated with prescribing without a documented qualifying indication among community-dwelling older adults across outpatient specialties. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of patients aged 65 or older with a qualifying outpatient antipsychotic dispensing at King Fahad Hospital of the University, Saudi Arabia, from January 2019 to May 2023. The index date was the first qualifying antipsychotic dispensing. A criteria-based algorithm classified each patient's prescribing appropriateness using FDA-approved indications, American Psychiatric Association guidelines, and the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with prescribing without a documented qualifying indication. RESULTS: Among 394 patients, clearly appropriate prescribing was identified in 16.0%, while dementia- or delirium-related prescribing was classified as high-risk/context-dependent in 18.8%. Documented off-label prescribing was identified in 11.2%, 48.0% had no documented qualifying indication, and 6.1% had no diagnosis recorded within the ascertainment window. The latter group was excluded from comparative analyses. In the regression sample (n = 370), prescribing without a documented qualifying indication was more likely when the index antipsychotic was prescribed by medical or primary care (AOR 4.43, 95% CI 2.00 to 9.81; p < 0.001), neurology (AOR 2.42, 95% CI 1.27 to 4.63; p = 0.007), or other departments (AOR 3.16, 95% CI 1.16 to 8.63; p = 0.025) than by psychiatry. CONCLUSION: Prescribing without a documented qualifying indication was common outside psychiatry, but the absence of a qualifying diagnosis in the records does not confirm inappropriate prescribing. Systematic indication documentation, medication review, and targeted stewardship may improve prescribing quality in older adults.

articles.title: Personalized Boolean network dynamic profiling and machine learning approaches to identify combinatorial treatments for prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed non-cutaneous cancer in males and the second leading cause of male cancer death in the United States. Androgen deprivation therapy to block androgen receptor (AR) signaling is part of the standard of care. However, approximately 30%-40% of patients experience biochemical recurrence (BCR) after primary therapy and progress to a more lethal form of castration-resistant prostate cancer for which there currently is no curative therapy. This study focused on patients at risk of progressing to BCR with the aim of identifying novel combinatorial targets that can be used with AR inhibition to provide greater therapeutic response. METHODS: Personalized Boolean network models were developed using The Cancer Genome Atlas and in-house data to integrate mutations, copy number alterations, and RNA-seq data. Asynchronous stochastic network simulations in MaBoSS (Markovian Boolean Stochastic Simulator) were used to identify potential drug targets in combination with AR inhibition, which were cross-checked using a machine learning algorithm and tested with a cytotoxicity assay across 4 prostate cancer cell lines. RESULTS: In silico predictions and in vitro experiments showed that target-specific co-inhibition of E2F1 or Cyclin B with an AR antagonist enhances enzalutamide-associated growth inhibition in all 4 prostate cancer cell lines. Pharmacodynamic modeling suggested that the drug combinations were synergistic with all interaction parameters estimated to be less than 1 (range = 0.156-0.834). DISCUSSION: Dynamic profiling of personalized Boolean networks in treatment-naïve prostate cancer subjects with and without BCR identified potential drug targets in combination with AR antagonists. Future xenograft studies are needed to confirm in vitro results, and exposure-response modeling could provide guidance for feasibility assessment and clinical trial design.

articles.title: Berberine and celecoxib synergistically suppress non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR/AKT/COX-2-related signaling: network pharmacology, molecular docking and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and safer combination strategies with improved antitumor efficacy are still needed. Berberine (BBR), a natural isoquinoline alkaloid with multi-target pharmacological activity, and celecoxib (CXB), a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor, have shown antitumor potential. However, their combined efficacy and underlying mechanisms in NSCLC remain unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology, molecular docking, Chou-Talalay combination index analysis, complementary synergy analysis using SynergyFinder+, in vitro functional assays, molecular validation, and a PC9 xenograft model were integrated to evaluate the antitumor effects and associated molecular changes of BBR combined with CXB. Candidate targets and pathways were screened using protein-protein interaction analysis, GO/KEGG enrichment, and Target-Pathway network analysis. Molecular docking was performed to assess the predicted binding affinity of BBR and CXB with key targets, and native-ligand re-docking was performed to validate the docking protocol. Cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, and molecular changes were examined using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell invasion, flow cytometry, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, immunohistochemistry, and in vivo experiments. RESULTS: Network analysis identified EGFR, AKT1, and PTGS2 (encoding COX-2) as candidate nodes, and molecular docking suggested predicted binding of BBR and CXB with EGFR, AKT1, and COX-2. Native-ligand re-docking showed acceptable reproduction of the crystallographic ligand poses. BBR and CXB synergistically reduced A549 and PC9 cell viability, with ZIP, HSA, Loewe, and Bliss analyses further supporting the multidose synergy, and a representative working combination dose was used for validation. The combination significantly inhibited proliferation, colony formation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. These effects were accompanied by suppression of EGFR and AKT phosphorylation, reduced COX-2 expression, downregulation of TNF-α, IL-1β, and CXCL8, decreased the Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and increased cleaved-Caspase-3. In vivo, BBR + CXB more effectively inhibited PC9 xenograft growth than either monotherapy without obvious body weight loss, accompanied by reduced Ki-67, p-EGFR, p-AKT, and COX-2 expression and increased cleaved-Caspase-3 staining. CONCLUSION: BBR combined with CXB exhibits synergistic antitumor activity in NSCLC cells and enhanced antitumor efficacy in vivo, associated with suppression of EGFR/AKT/COX-2-related signaling, attenuation of inflammatory responses, and activation of apoptosis, providing support for this potential combination strategy.

articles.title: Zhuyu pill relieves cholestasis in rats by modulating the expression of lncRNAs and circRNAs.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Zhuyu pill (ZYP), a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula composed of Coptis chinensis Franch and Tetradium ruticarpum (A. Jussieu) T. G. Hartley, exhibiting potential anti-cholestatic effects. However, its specific mechanism remains unclear. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs) are critical gene expression regulators and promising direction for exploring the mechanism. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to validate the anti-cholestatic effects of ZYP and explore its potential biological mechanisms through lncRNAs and circRNAs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats with alpha-naphthyl isothiocyanate (ANIT)-induced cholestasis were treated with low-dose (0.6 g/kg) or high-dose (1.2 g/kg) ZYP. Efficacy was assessed by serum biochemistry and histopathology. Differentially expressed lncRNAs (DElncRNAs) and circRNAs (DEcircRNAs) in liver tissues were identified via RNA sequencing, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. MiRanda was used to predict DElncRNAs/DEcircRNAs-miRNA interactions and construct interaction networks. Subsequently, trend analysis was used to screen lncRNA/circRNA-miRNA pairs with expression patterns consistent with the competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory mechanism. RESULTS: Both high- and low-dose ZYP significantly improved biochemical and histopathological parameters, with the high-dose group showing superior effects. Enrichment analysis showed that DElncRNA-related functions were mainly concentrated in lipid metabolism pathways ("Bile secretion", "Adipocytokine signaling pathway", "Arachidonic acid metabolism") and inflammation-related pathways ("NF-κB", "TNF", "MAPK", and "Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)"), suggesting their roles in alleviating inflammatory injury and lipid metabolism disorders. Among these, core lncRNAs altered by ANIT and reversed by ZYP included TCONS_00032614, TCONS_00018259, TCONS_00025702, TCONS_00012591, and TCONS_00003751, with qRT-PCR results largely consistent with sequencing data. Further lncRNA-miRNA binding prediction and expression trend analysis identified candidate pairs with potential competing ceRNA characteristics: TCONS_00003751/rno-miR-328b-3p, TCONS_00003751/rno-miR-328a-3p, and TCONS_00032614/rno-miR-149-5p. Similarly, DEcircRNA-associated pathways were enriched in inflammatory and immune responses ("Cell adhesion molecules (CAMs)", "Antigen processing and presentation", and "Cytochrome P450 metabolism of xenobiotics"). Candidate circRNAs included circRNA_1402 and circRNA_1452, and Candidate pairs with potential competing ceRNA characteristics included circRNA_1402/rno-miR-1306-5p and circRNA_1452/rno-miR-23a-5p. CONCLUSION: ZYP dose-dependently improved biochemical and histopathological parameters in cholestatic rats. This effect is closely related to the roles of lncRNAs and circRNAs in regulating lipid metabolism and inflammation-related pathways. Several candidate ceRNA pairs were preliminarily screened, yet further experimental validation is warranted.

articles.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis. METHODS: We applied two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based MR, and Bayesian colocalization to evaluate the associations of genetically proxied levels of 213 lipid-lowering drug target proteins with lumbar spinal stenosis risk. Candidate targets were evaluated via genetic immune-cell mediation analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: MR identified three proteins increasing disease risk, with placental alkaline phosphatase (ALPP) consistently replicating across platforms (colocalization at rs12478529, PP.H4 = 0.9979). Genetically inferred mediation analysis suggested that selected immune-cell traits may partially mediate the association between ALPP and lumbar spinal stenosis. Molecular dynamics simulations and cellular thermal shift assays supported target engagement of atorvastatin and simvastatin with ALPP. In clinical specimens, ALPP was upregulated in hypertrophied tissues, co-localizing with fibrosis and lipid accumulation. In vitro, statins suppressed lipid accumulation and fibrotic markers; ALPP overexpression counteracted these protective effects. In vivo, systemic statin administration attenuated ligamentum flavum thickening, whereas local viral-mediated ALPP overexpression reversed this benefit. CONCLUSION: Our findings identify ALPP as a genetically supported candidate associated with LSS and link it to lipid accumulation and fibrosis. Computational and CETSA findings support possible target engagement of statins with ALPP and attenuate lipid accumulation and fibrosis, supporting ALPP as a potential mediator of their effects and statin repurposing for LSS.

articles.title: Statistical process control within the Six Sigma DMAIC framework for monitoring medication dispensing errors in hospital pharmacies: a Saudi case study.
articles.abstract: This study employed the Six Sigma DMAIC methodology to monitor and analyze medication dispensing errors in hospital pharmacies in Saudi Arabia, with a focus on Mecca and Jeddah cities. Using aggregated data from the Ministry of Health (MOH) Statistical Yearbook 2024, a synthetic dataset was generated through a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) to enable the Statistical Process Control (SPC) analysis. The p-chart application demonstrated how process stability can be evaluated within a synthetic healthcare dataset, while the calculated sigma level (2.49) represents the performance characteristics of the generated data rather than actual hospital pharmacy performance. Pareto analysis illustrated how dominant error categories can be prioritized within a synthetic dataset generated under predefined assumptions. Based on these findings, several improvement strategies were proposed, particularly targeting dispensing errors within pharmacy operations. However, due to the use of synthetic data, the improvement and control phases remain conceptual. The generated synthetic dataset enabled demonstration of Statistical Process Control (SPC) techniques within the Six Sigma DMAIC framework. The p-chart indicated statistical stability within the generated data, while Pareto analysis illustrated the prioritization of error categories under predefined synthetic distributions. Because all analyses were conducted using CTGAN-generated synthetic records, the findings should be interpreted as a methodological demonstration rather than as evidence of actual medication error performance in Saudi hospital pharmacies.

articles.title: Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses.
