This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP). METHODS: GFP-GP pulldown coupled with co-immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry was used to identify GP-associated host candidates. A PSMD11/Rpn6-centred workflow integrated knowledge-graph inference, ligand-only machine learning, ADMETlab profiling and interface-guided docking. Candidate prioritization was assessed through score-weight sensitivity analysis, applicability-domain assessment and docking controls addressing seed reproducibility, search convergence, whole-receptor context and macrocycle ring-conformer sensitivity. Docking scores were contextualized against a matched 59-compound library. RESULTS: The analysis recovered 424 GP-pulldown-specific host proteins and nominated PSMD11/Rpn6 as a proteostasis anchor. The tier-gated knowledge-graph candidate membership was invariant across the tested weight perturbations, with Spearman rho = 0.998 under equal weighting. The selected ExtraTrees model achieved an AUC of 0.912 for the Ki endpoint. Applicability-domain assessment and ADMET profiling differentiated candidate confidence and predicted liabilities. Docking reproducibility checks yielded a maximum standard deviation of 0.05 kcal/mol for conformationally restricted ligands, while macrocyclic candidates showed greater protocol-dependent variability. Rule-based triage integrating upstream evidence, ADMET burden, chemotype diversity and mechanistic coverage returned five candidates: betamethasone, bafilomycin A1, everolimus, pitavastatin and CHEMBL1410015. DISCUSSION: The workflow links a proteomic host-factor signal to a compact set of chemically diverse hypotheses with explicit evidence sources and limitations. The candidates remain hypotheses for experimental assessment; direct target engagement, interface blockade and antiviral activity are not established by the present study.

articles.title: Safety signals and CMV-related events reported during letermovir therapy: a FAERS database study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Letermovir is an antiviral agent approved for CMV infection prophylaxis in transplant recipients. This study aimed to evaluate safety signals reported during letermovir treatment, using data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). METHODS: Data from October 2017 to September 2024 were extracted from FAERS database. Reported events were analyzed across hierarchy levels, from Preferred Term (PT) to High-Level Terms (HLTs) and System Organ Classes (SOCs). Disproportionality analysis was performed to detect safety signals. Recorded time to onset was analyzed descriptively, and univariable logistic regression was performed to explore report-level factors. RESULTS: The most frequently reported events was infections and infestations at SOC level, cytomegalovirus infection at HLT level and CMV infection reactivation at Preferred Term level. Apart from CMV-related events, safety signals involved hematological abnormalities, pericardial effusion, hepatic and renal failure, bacterial and viral infections, pathogen resistance, and transplantation-related events. The median recorded time to onset was 25 days for all events, and 33 days for CMV-related events, with later recorded onset in intravenous than tablet reports. Exploratory logistic regression showed lower odds of CMV-related event reporting with older age and treatment initiation in more recent years, higher odds with intravenous administration, and regional differences in reporting. CONCLUSION: This study identified safety signals reported with letermovir involving hematological, cardiac, hepatic, renal, infectious, and transplantation-related events. CMV-related signals may reflect breakthrough infection. These findings require validation in clinical studies.

articles.title: Case report: Butylphthalide-associated severe thrombocytopenia, a rare adverse drug reaction.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Butylphthalide (DL-NBP) is a widely used neuroprotective agent for acute ischemic stroke. Although generally well-tolerated, severe thrombocytopenia as a rare adverse reaction has not been fully recognized. Herein, we report a severe case of probable DL-NBP-associated thrombocytopenia to increase clinical awareness and inform clinical management. CASE PRESENTATION: A 69-year-old male with hypertension was admitted for acute brainstem infarction. His hospitalization was complicated by catastrophic thrombocytopenia (min 1.0 × 109/L), suggestive of a possible immune-mediated thrombocytopenia. Subsequent complications included hypoxemia, pneumonia, occult gastrointestinal blood loss, and muscular venous thrombosis of the right calf, creating complex management challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration, multimodal tailored treatment was delivered to balance the risks of stroke recurrence and bleeding: corticosteroids, platelet transfusion, recombinant human thrombopoietin and recombinant human interleukin-11 were administered for presumed immune-mediated thrombocytopenia, and antiplatelet therapy was sequentially modified. The patient's condition stabilized with normalized platelet counts, and he was transferred for rehabilitation. CONCLUSION: Severe thrombocytopenia showed a temporal association with DL-NBP treatment. After excluding alternative etiologies, probable DL-NBP-associated thrombocytopenia was considered in this case.

articles.title: Enlicitide: The First Oral PCSK9i for Lowering Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This article describes pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy data of enlicitide, the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor (PCSK9i). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through July 17, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Clinical trials published in English were included. Relevant information from the methodology and results was extracted. DATA SYNTHESIS: Enlicitide received FDA approval on July 16, 2026, based on results from phase 2 and 3 trials showing a 57.1% to 64.6% reduction in low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) and reduced other atherogenic lipid particles at 24 weeks in patients with hypercholesterolemia, including those with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, while maintaining a favorable adverse effect profile. Enlicitide represents the fifth FDA-approved agent targeting PCSK9, having similar efficacy to other agents in class while having a novel macrocyclic peptide formulation with permeation enhancers, allowing for oral administration.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:As PCSK9is continue to be at the forefront of dyslipidemia guidelines, the approval of an oral agent is paramount in ensuring patient access. Enlicitide mirrors LDL-C lowering compared with existing PCSK9is and surpasses LDL-C lowering compared with non-statin options such as bempedoic acid and ezetimibe. Confirmation of cardiovascular outcomes data with enlicitide will solidify its role in reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. CONCLUSION: Enlicitide significantly lowered LDL-C similar to existing PCSK9is with few adverse effects. The oral formulation provides an essential option for LDL-C lowering, especially in patients adverse to injections.

articles.title: Ritlecitinib in Nonsegmental Vitiligo: A Systematic Review and Comprehensive Program Synthesis of Clinical Efficacy, Safety, and Biomarker Outcomes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of oral ritlecitinib, a selective Janus kinase 3 (JAK3) and tyrosine kinase expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (TEC) family kinase inhibitor, for the treatment of nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV). DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 31, 2026. Search terms included combinations of "ritlecitinib," "JAK inhibitor," and "vitiligo.." STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Included studies were clinical trials evaluating ritlecitinib, monotherapy, or with narrowband ultraviolet B (nbUVB), in adults with NSV. Five interrelated studies from the ritlecitinib phase 2b program involving 364 participants were identified for qualitative synthesis. Data extraction included study design, participant demographics, efficacy indices (F-VASI[Facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index], T-VASI [Total Vitiligo Area Scoring Index], and PGIC-V [Patient Global Impression of Change-Vitiligo]), biomarker changes, and safety outcomes. Quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool. DATA SYNTHESIS: Ritlecitinib 50 mg daily demonstrated significant facial repigmentation at week 24, achieving a percent change from baseline (%CFB) in F-VASI of -18.5% to -21.2% compared with +2.1% for placebo. Adding nbUVB significantly enhanced efficacy (F-VASI %CFB: -69.6% vs -55.1%; P = .009) and total-body repigmentation. Darker skin phototypes (FST IV-VI) showed earlier and more robust responses (-37.4%) than lighter skin types (FST I-III; -15.2%). Safety outcomes were comparable with placebo, with overall adverse event rates between 60.0% and 86.2% and rare serious adverse events (≤2%). Biomarker analysis confirmed the downregulation of Th1-associated markers (CXCL9 and IFNG) and restoration of melanocyte markers like tyrosinase and Melan-A.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Ritlecitinib 50 mg daily provides a well-tolerated oral systemic option for active NSV. Efficacy is optimized when combined with nbUVB, and baseline skin phototype is a key predictor of the speed and extent of repigmentation. CONCLUSIONS: Oral ritlecitinib 50 mg daily is an effective systemic treatment for active NSV, demonstrating continuous repigmentation through 48 weeks with a favorable safety profile.

articles.title: Low-Dose Buprenorphine Initiation Strategies for Pain.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this review is to describe the common benefits and pitfalls of various low-dose buprenorphine initiation strategies for patients experiencing long-term pain without opioid use disorder (OUD). DATA SOURCES: A search of the primary literature was performed in PubMed using the following keywords: "Buprenorphine OR Buprenorphine-naloxone OR Belbuca OR Suboxone, Primary care OR Outpatient, Pain OR Pain management," from January 1980 to August 2, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Case reports involving the use of sublingual/buccal buprenorphine in outpatients for pain without OUD were included. DATA SYNTHESIS: Three low-dose buprenorphine initiation methods were evaluated, titrating buprenorphine from once to thrice-daily up to a total of 7 days. Two studies abruptly discontinued full μ-agonists prior to initiating buprenorphine, whereas 1 study tapered full μ-agonists by 25% weekly after day 7. Tapering full-agonist opioids after attainment of target buprenorphine dosing was well tolerated and potentially unneeded after steady-state levels were achieved; bridging analgesia with sufficient pharmacokinetic overlap between buprenorphine and full μ-agonist opioids appears tantamount to mitigating withdrawal symptoms. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: The ideal buprenorphine initiation method considers desired duration, whether to perform cross-titration, product pharmacokinetics, patient-specific factors, and goals of care. CONCLUSIONS: No data exist to support one low-dose buprenorphine initiation method over another. All methods discussed were highly successful at rotating patients to buprenorphine, that is, with equivalent or improved pain control with minimal to no withdrawal symptoms and may be used to build a methodology for starting buprenorphine in outpatients with sub-optimal pain regimens.

articles.title: Hermann Kappus (16 Oct 1944-10 July 2026).
The Potential Impact of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors on Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are widely prescribed for mood disorders. Their association with musculoskeletal side effects raises the question of potential SSRI impact on exercise-induced muscle damage and recovery. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this prospective cohort study was to determine if SSRI use influences muscle function following a bout of eccentric exercise designed to induce delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). METHODS: Subjects between 18 and 30 years of age were recruited in a university setting. This included 1 group taking SSRIs prescribed by their health care provider, and a control group not using SSRIs. Subjects performed a DOMS induction protocol consisting of 300 eccentric knee extensions on an isokinetic dynamometer. Muscle soreness, thigh circumference, quadriceps flexibility, and isometric quadriceps strength were measured at baseline and at 24-, 48-, 72-, and 96-hour post-DOMS protocol. Comparisons were made between SSRI users and control subjects. RESULTS: Thirty-six subjects included 18 SSRI users and 18 controls. The DOMS protocol induced muscle soreness in both groups (P < .001 when compared with baseline). At 72 hours a between-group difference was observed for thigh muscle flexibility (MD = 11.2, SE = 5.0, 95% CI [0.9, 21.4], P = .033, ηp2 = .126) but no additional significant between-group differences in soreness, strength, thigh circumference, or flexibility were noted at any timepoint. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this population, SSRI use had no effect on muscle soreness, circumference, or strength of the quadriceps following eccentric DOMS-inducing exercise. A difference in flexibility between SSRI and control groups at a single time point likely reflects a Type 1 error and is not likely of clinical consequence. These findings suggest SSRIs do not impair short-term recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage in healthy young adults, but potential SSRI impacts on longer-term training adaptations and recovery in athletic populations remain unknown.

articles.title: Therapeutic Potential of Flavonoids and Their Metabolites in Hyperlipidaemia: Molecular Mechanisms, Bioavailability and Clinical Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Hyperlipidaemia is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and remains a global health concern. Although conventional lipid-lowering drugs are effective, their long-term use is often associated with adverse effects, prompting interest in safer dietary alternatives. Flavonoids, such as quercetin, naringenin, and catechins, have gained attention for their hypolipidemic and cardioprotective properties. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of quercetin, catechins, naringenin, and their bioactive metabolites in the management of hyperlipidaemia. The literature was identified through comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and March 2026 using combinations of the keywords flavonoids, quercetin, catechins, naringenin, metabolites, hyperlipidaemia, dyslipidaemia, lipid metabolism, cardiovascular disease, and gut microbiota. Original research articles, clinical studies, experimental investigations, and high-quality review articles published in English were considered, while duplicate, non-English, and unrelated reports were excluded from the study. Evidence indicates that flavonoids and their metabolites modulate multiple pathways involved in lipid homeostasis, including the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, activation of AMPK and PPARα, suppression of SREBP-1c, enhancement of LDL receptor expression, regulation of gut microbiota, and attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation. Despite encouraging preclinical and clinical findings, limited bioavailability, extensive metabolism, inter-individual variability, and insufficient long-term clinical evidence remain important challenges. Overall, flavonoids and their metabolites represent promising adjunctive dietary strategies for improving lipid metabolism and reducing cardiovascular risk. However, welldesigned randomized clinical trials and advanced delivery systems are needed to establish their therapeutic efficacy and clinical applicability.

articles.title: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Graves' Disease: Current Advances and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Graves' Disease (GD) is the leading cause of autoimmune hyperthyroidism and is still considered a challenging clinical condition. Antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine, and thyroidectomy have long been used as main treatments. These approaches are generally effective in restoring euthyroidism and controlling thyroid function, even if they cannot target the underlying autoimmune mechanisms implicated in the disease. As a result, relapses after medical therapy remain frequent, whereas definitive treatments often lead to permanent hypothyroidism and the need for a lifelong thyroid hormone replacement. New results in the study of immunological mechanisms underlying GD have led to the development of targeted therapies. Targeted strategies are based on key components of disease pathogenesis, such as the thyrotropin receptor, B lymphocytes, co-stimulatory immune pathways, the insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor, and neonatal Fc receptors. A pivotal step in the development of targeted mechanism-based therapies for GD has been reached with the approval of teprotumumab. Several targeted therapies have been evaluated, such as K1-70, iscalimab, rituximab, tocilizumab, batoclimab, and the antigen-specific immunotherapy ATX-GD-59. This review highlights the limitations of currently available treatment options by examining the most promising emerging therapies and the future horizons for precision medicine in GD. Advances in the therapeutic landscape offer disease-modifying strategies that could complement and potentially replace current treatment strategies.

articles.title: Diindolylmethane Pretreatment Attenuated Thioacetamide-Induced Acute Liver Failure and its Associated Brain Injury in Rats.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute liver failure (ALF) is a life-threatening condition associated with hepatic encephalopathy (HE), characterised by neurological impairments, hyperammonemia, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Diindolylmethane (DIM), a bioactive compound derived from cruciferous vegetables, has shown potential hepatoprotective and neuroprotective effects via its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Despite beneficial effects, its protective effects have not been investigated against HE. The present study evaluated the hepatoprotective and neuroprotective effects of DIM in a rat model of thioacetamide (TAA)- induced ALF and HE. METHODS: ALF was induced using thioacetamide (TAA; 300 mg/kg, i.p.). DIM at doses of 12.5, 25, and 50 mg/kg, p.o., was administered for 7 days prior to TAA injection. Behavioral assessments, including the open field test and Y-maze, were performed to evaluate motor and cognitive functions. Biochemical parameters (AST, ALT, ALP, and LDH), ammonia levels, oxidative stress markers (MDA, NRF2, SOD, GSH, and catalase), inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10), and apoptotic markers (cytochrome c, caspase 9, and caspase 3) were analysed. Histopathological examinations of the liver, cortex, and hippocampus were conducted using hematoxylin and eosin staining. RESULTS: DIM pretreatment significantly reduced liver enzyme levels (AST, ALT, ALP, and LDH), normalised organ weight ratios, and decreased ammonia levels in blood, liver, and brain. DIM attenuated oxidative stress by reducing MDA levels and enhancing NRF2, SOD, GSH, and catalase activity, suggesting its antioxidant potential. Further, DIM reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels and increased IL-10 levels, indicating its antiinflammatory effects. Furthermore, DIM reduced the apoptotic markers, including cytochrome c, caspase 9, and caspase 3, suggesting attenuation of apoptosis. Additionally, DIM improved motor activity and spatial memory and exhibited an anxiolytic effect. DIM mitigated the TAA-induced liver, hippocampal, and cortical tissue abnormalities. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that DIM exerts protective effects against ALF-induced HE by modulating key pathological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis. The reduction in hyperammonemia and restoration of biochemical and behavioral parameters indicate its potential role in preserving liver and brain function. CONCLUSION: DIM demonstrates significant hepatoprotective and neuroprotective effects in TAA-induced ALF and HE. These effects are mediated through multiple mechanisms, suggesting DIM as a potential therapeutic candidate for managing ALF-associated neurological complications. Future studies require investigating the in-depth mechanism of DIM against HE.

articles.title: UPLC-Q-TOF/MS, Network Pharmacology, and Experimental Validation Reveal the Mechanisms of Shuangbai Tablet Against Albuminuria.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Shuangbai Tablet (SBT), a traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated efficacy in reducing albuminuria. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic mechanisms underlying its antialbuminuric effects. METHODS: The phytochemicals of SBT were analyzed by UPLC-Q-TOF/MS. Subsequently, we crossvalidated the identified phytochemicals and predicted the potential targets of SBT for albuminuria by network pharmacology and molecular docking analysis. Albuminuric male Wistar rats were induced by a single tailvein injection of Adriamycin (ADR, 5 mg/kg) and orally administered SBT for 8 weeks. Then, 24-hour Urine Protein (24 h-UTP) and serum albumin were assessed, along with changes in renal function, systemic lipid metabolism, and serum COX-2 levels. Renal histopathology was evaluated by H&E staining, while the renal expressions of VEGFR-1, VEGFA, HIF-1α, NF-κB p65, ACTN-4, and podocin were assessed by immunohistochemistry and western blotting. RESULTS: Nine core active phytochemicals of SBT targeting HIF-1α and VEGFA were identified for albuminuria treatment. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding affinities between these phytochemicals and both HIF-1α and VEGFA. In ADR-treated rats, SBT significantly reduced proteinuria (24 h-UTP: 245.1 (95% CI, 174.9 to 315.3) mg/24 h in the middle-dose SBT group vs. 585.2 (95% CI, 460.0 to 710.4) mg/24 h in the ADR group; p < 0.0001), reversed hypoalbuminemia (ALB: 24.44 (95% CI, 17.62 to 31.25) g/L vs. 9.70 (95% CI, 4.94 to 14.46) g/L; p < 0.05), ameliorated renal dysfunction and lipid metabolic disturbances, and suppressed serum COX-2 levels. Histopathological analysis showed ameliorated renal injury. SBT stabilized the decreased expressions of renal VEGFR-1, VEGFA, HIF-1α, ACTN-4, and podocin, while suppressing NF-κB p65expression. DISCUSSION: Further functional characterization studies are warranted to validate the pharmacological effects of SBT on albuminuria. CONCLUSION: SBT can alleviate albuminuria, inflammation, and renal injury, associated with the stabilization of HIF-1α and VEGFA expressions.

articles.title: Rational Use of Analgesic Agents in Elderly Patients: Implications of the Beers Criteria and STOPP/START Algorithms.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Pain affects approximately 30% of community-dwelling older adults and more than half of nursing-home residents but remains undertreated because age-related pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes render standard analgesic dosing hazardous. This review synthesises the evidence on rational analgesic prescribing in older adults, comparing the American Geriatrics Society 2023 Beers Criteria with STOPP/START version 3. METHODS: In this structured narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2000-May 2026), combining analgesic-class terms with the Beers Criteria, STOPP/START, potentially inappropriate medications, deprescribing and older age. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomised trials, large observational studies and guidelines in English were eligible; studies confined to patients younger than 65 years were excluded. RESULTS: Analgesics are principal drivers of inappropriate prescribing: STOPP/START version 3 identified at least one potentially inappropriate medication in 73% of geriatric outpatients versus 56% under version 2, NSAIDs and aspirin being the most prevalent new criteria. The Beers Criteria designate meperidine, non-selective oral NSAIDs, anticholinergic tricyclic antidepressants, and opioid-benzodiazepine or opioidgabapentinoid combinations as highest risk; meperidine is most strongly associated with unplanned hospitalisation (OR 2.37). DISCUSSION: The instruments are complementary, not interchangeable: the Beers Criteria offer broader drug-disease coverage but are aligned with the United States formulary, whereas STOPP/START is bidirectional and more prescriptive on dose and renal thresholds. Neither has been shown to reduce falls, hospitalisation or mortality in adequately powered trials. CONCLUSION: Stepwise multimodal analgesia beginning with paracetamol and topical agents, initiated at low doses and titrated slowly, with comprehensive geriatric assessment and regular medication review, remains the evidence-based standard of care.

articles.title: Assessment of the Effects of Corporate Governance on the Competitiveness of Pharmaceutical Companies Through Improved Total Factor Productivity.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Corporate governance, productivity, and competitiveness are widely recognized as key determinants of firm performance and long-term sustainability. Although each construct has been extensively studied individually, their interrelationships, particularly within the pharmaceutical industry of developing economies, remain insufficiently understood. This gap is especially relevant given the strategic and economic importance of the pharmaceutical sector. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the relationships among corporate governance, competitiveness, and productivity in Iranian pharmaceutical companies and to develop a model that better explains the interactions among these determinants. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in three phases among Iranian pharmaceutical manufacturing companies. First, context-specific, validated questionnaires were developed to assess corporate governance, productivity, and competitiveness. Second, these instruments were administered to senior executives (Chief Executive Officers [CEOs], board members, Chief Financial Officers [CFOs], and Chief Commercial Officers [CCOs]) at 44 randomly selected companies. Finally, statistical analyses, including Pearson and partial correlations, independent t-tests, and bootstrapped mediation analysis, were performed to evaluate the relationships among the study variables. RESULTS: A total of 151 completed questionnaires were analyzed (response rate: 85.8%). Productivity showed a strong positive correlation with competitiveness (r = 0.780, P < 0.001) and a moderate positive correlation with corporate governance (r = 0.419, P = 0.005). By contrast, no significant direct correlation was observed between corporate governance and competitiveness. Mediation analysis indicated that productivity mediated the relationship between corporate governance and competitiveness, indicating a substantial indirect effect. In addition, companies producing biological medicines had significantly higher productivity and competitiveness scores. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest a partially interdependent model in which corporate governance enhances competitiveness primarily through its positive effect on productivity rather than through a direct pathway. Strengthening governance structures to improve decision-making and resource utilization may therefore be an effective strategy for increasing productivity and, ultimately, competitiveness in the pharmaceutical industry.

articles.title: Yishen Xiaoke Formula Delays Renal Fibrosis in Rats with Diabetic Nephropathy by Suppressing the Transforming Growth Factor-Beta 1/Notch Signalling Pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Yishen Xiaoke Formula (YSXKF), derived from the classical prescription Yuquan San, has been used clinically to treat diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with qi-yin deficiency syndrome. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether YSXKF delays renal fibrosis progression in DN rats by regulating the transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1)/Notch signalling pathway. METHODS: Seventy-five male Sprague Dawley rats were included and randomly assigned to a control cohort (15 rats) or a model cohort (60 rats). DN was induced by unilateral nephrectomy, a high-fat/high-sucrose diet, and streptozotocin injection. DN rats were treated with YSXKF, irbesartan, or YSXKF combined with TGF-β1 activation for 8 weeks. After 8 weeks of intervention, 24-h urinary total protein (24-h UTP), circulating TGF-β1 levels, fasting blood glucose (FBG), and serum creatinine (Scr) were evaluated. Masson staining was performed to assess renal pathological changes, and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry were conducted to assess the levels of TGF-β1, Jagged1, and Hes1 in renal tissue. RESULTS: Compared with DN rats, YSXKF treatment significantly reduced 24-h UTP excretion, circulating TGF-β1 levels, FBG, and Scr. Histological analysis revealed attenuated glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis. YSXKF decreased renal mRNA and protein expression of TGF-β1, Jagged1, and Hes1. Activation of TGF-β1 markedly reversed these protective effects and restored Notch pathway activation. CONCLUSIONS: YSXKF delays renal fibrosis progression in DN rats by downregulating TGF-β1 expression and inhibiting Jagged1/Hes1 activation in the Notch signaling pathway, thereby reducing extracellular matrix deposition.

articles.title: Editorial: Shaping the future of predictive toxicology: addressing challenges and new approach methodologies.
Editorial: Exploring untapped potential: innovations in drug repurposing.
Manufacturing Quality Issues in Healthcare and Cosmetics: An Analysis of FDA Surveillance Data.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Poor manufacturing quality in healthcare and cosmetic products expose people to danger and needs further categorization and assessment. OBJECTIVE: This study reviewed Food and Drug Administration (FDA) records to identify major types of quality issues, the type of products involved, and patterns occurring over time. METHODS: The "FDA Health Fraud Product" and "FDA Recalls, Market Withdrawals, and Safety Alerts" databases were assessed from June 4, 2010, through May 30, 2026. Drugs, cosmetics, and dietary supplements/quasi-legal products with verified manufacturing quality issues were included. Products were sorted by product type and FDA warning letters or official reports were reviewed and categorized. RESULTS: Of 266 reviewed entries, 195 manufacturing quality issues were elucidated from 184 unique products. Drugs accounted for 70% of issues, cosmetics for 21%, and dietary supplement/quasi-legal products for 9%, respectively. Overall, chemical contamination (30%), procedural or testing issues (29%), and microbial contamination (19%) comprised 78% of identified issues. Drug issues were primarily procedural/testing, chemical contamination, and microbial contamination; cosmetic issues were predominantly elemental impurities and chemical contamination; and dietary supplement/quasi-legal issues were mainly microbial contamination, procedural/testing, and elemental impurities. Particulate contamination occurred only in drugs. The number of issues per year showed no consistent trend, but spiked in 2020, 2022, 2024, and 2025. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Manufacturing quality problems varied substantially by product category and occurred in irregular clusters. Inconsistent FDA reporting practices and fluctuations in agency surveillance may have contributed to these patterns. Budgetary cuts to the FDA could increase consumer exposure to manufacturing issues.

articles.title: Is it safe-and ethical-to prescribe THC to youth?
articles.abstract: The medical use of cannabis-derived products in children and adolescents has expanded beyond established indications for purified cannabidiol (CBD), with increasing investigation of CBD-rich extracts containing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) for neuropsychiatric conditions. Although preliminary studies suggest potential symptomatic benefits, the evidence remains limited by small samples, heterogeneous formulations, short follow-up, and insufficient assessment of long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes. Unlike CBD, THC directly activates CB1 receptors as a partial agonist, a pharmacological property underlying both its therapeutic and psychoactive effects. Following oral administration, THC undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism to the psychoactive metabolite 11-hydroxy-THC, with substantial interindividual variability in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics supporting individualized dosing according to clinical response and tolerability. Experimental studies raise concerns regarding THC exposure during neurodevelopment, while observational studies associate frequent, high-potency recreational cannabis use with cognitive impairment, psychosis, and other adverse psychiatric outcomes. These findings cannot be directly extrapolated to regulated medicinal cannabinoid use, which differs substantially in product composition, dosing, administration, therapeutic indication, and clinical monitoring. Nevertheless, long-term neurodevelopmental safety data for medicinal THC exposure in children and adolescents remain limited. These uncertainties must be weighed against the consequences of inadequately treated disease, particularly severe drug-resistant epilepsy. Accordingly, the risk-benefit assessment of THC-containing products should be individualized, considering disease severity, treatment refractoriness, available evidence-based alternatives, therapeutic response, and tolerability. Long-term prospective studies and improved patient-selection strategies are needed to better define the role of THC-containing medicinal products in pediatric populations.
